findings.title: Distinct agent identity
findings.requirement: Give the agent its own non-human identity. Keep it separate from the user who launched it and from unrelated agents. Show that permissions and revocation belong to that identity, even when a user starts the run.

not_covered.problem: Action records missing any of the six identity fields
Instance or tenant labels taken from what the model supplies
A credential scoped to more operations, resources, or tenants than needed
Revocation delay from cached or self-contained tokens not measured

checks.check: The agent runs under its own workload principal (service account, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID) that no other service or unrelated agent uses.
checks.verify: 1) Find the agent's identity: pod `serviceAccountName`, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID in IaC or deploy config. 2) Search other deployments, services, and agents in the repo for the same name or role. 3) Answer no if it is shared, `default`, the main backend's identity, or only a string label with no credential. Answer unknown if identity is assigned outside this repo.

checks.check: Tool and API clients get credentials from the agent's own principal, not from the launching user's forwarded token or session cookie.
checks.verify: 1) Find every place tool and API clients get a token or key. 2) Trace where each comes from: workload identity or token exchange, versus the incoming request's `Authorization` header or session cookie. 3) Check every client, not just the main one. 4) Answer no if any client forwards the user's token or cookie as-is, or uses a shared static key.

checks.check: When a user starts a run, the user is carried as a delegated subject (for example a token exchange with separate act and sub), while the agent keeps its own principal.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code that starts a run for a user. 2) Look for token exchange (RFC 8693, `subject_token`, `actor_token`, `act`/`sub` claims) or a separate delegated-subject field. 3) Check the agent's own principal is still the actor. 4) Answer no if the user's token is used directly or the user replaces the agent identity. Answer unknown if the exchange happens in an outside identity service.

checks.check: Permissions are bound to the agent principal in IaC or RBAC, so revoking that principal alone removes the agent's access without disabling the user.
checks.verify: 1) Find IAM policies, RoleBindings, or grants in Terraform, Helm, or Kubernetes YAML. 2) Check they bind to the agent principal, not to a user, group, or shared role. 3) Check that removing that binding alone would cut the agent's access. 4) Answer no if access depends on the user's grants or a shared credential. Answer unknown if permissions are not defined in this repo.

findings.title: All six identity fields
findings.requirement: Check that every action records the accountable party, operational owner, tenant, agent-type-id, agent-instance-id, and trace context. Look at successful, denied, failed, and background actions, not just the main request path.

not_covered.problem: Identity labels taken from what the model supplies
Agent-type-id not computed as a hash of its identity inputs
Agent able to erase or rewrite its own audit history
Sub-agent record missing its parent link or parent prompt

checks.check: The audit record schema has all six fields: accountable party, operational owner, tenant, agent-type-id, agent-instance-id, and trace context.
checks.verify: 1) Find the audit record schema or the function that writes audit entries. 2) Check for each of the six: accountable party, operational owner, tenant, `agent.type.id`, `agent.instance.id`, trace context (`traceparent` or trace and span IDs). 3) Answer no if any one is missing from the schema or never set.

checks.check: All six fields are written on denied, failed, async, and background actions too, not only on the successful main request path.
checks.verify: 1) List every path that writes an audit record, or should: success, policy deny, `except`/`catch` blocks, retries, queue workers, cron jobs, webhooks, other endpoints such as approvals, and refusals before the run starts (quota, rate limit, auth) that return an error without logging. 2) For each, check all six fields are set, ideally by one shared wrapper. 3) Answer no if any deny, error, async, or background path writes records without them, or writes no record at all.

checks.check: Trace context (trace and span IDs) is stored in the audit record itself, not only in separate tracing spans.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record writer. 2) Check it stores trace and span IDs (or `traceparent`) as fields in the record itself. 3) Answer no if trace context exists only in OpenTelemetry spans, or the record's trace field is never filled.

checks.check: Tenant and owner values come from the trusted layer, not from baggage, tracestate, or other unprotected headers.
checks.verify: 1) Find where tenant and owner values for audit records are read. 2) Trace each back to its source: token claims, verified session, IAM tags, or SPIFFE path, versus OTel baggage, `tracestate`, headers like `X-Tenant-Id`, request body, or tool arguments. 3) Answer no if any path takes them from an unprotected source.

findings.title: Content-derived type identity
findings.requirement: Compute the agent-type-id as a hash of the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration. The model part includes checkpoint and fine-tune or adapter references where they apply. Keep the list of inputs (the manifest) and the hashing steps. Check that changing any input changes the ID, and that the same manifest gives the same ID.

not_covered.problem: Changed running config still reporting the old approved ID
Hosted model changing behind a fixed name
Release manifest missing training job, dataset, or model provider records
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

checks.check: The agent-type-id is a hash over a manifest that includes the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code or CI step that computes `agent.type.id` (search `sha256`, `hashlib`, `createHash`, `type_id`). 2) List its inputs. 3) Check each is there: container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, configuration. 4) Answer no if the ID is a label, version string, or git tag, or any input is missing.

checks.check: The hash covers every file that defines the prompt, tools, and configuration, with no file or directory skipped or excluded.
checks.verify: 1) Open the function that lists files to hash. 2) Write down every filter it applies: hidden files, names starting with '_' or '__', extensions, ignore lists, glob patterns. 3) For each filter, check whether a file that defines tools, prompts, or config would be skipped (for example `__init__.py`, `index.ts`, `.env`, `config/*.local.*`). 4) Answer no if any such file is skipped.

checks.check: The model input is a pinned version or snapshot (plus checkpoint and adapter references where used), not an alias and not the app's release number.
checks.verify: 1) Find the model ID that goes into the manifest or hash. 2) Follow env vars and config to the final value, including defaults such as `getenv('MODEL', ...)`. 3) Answer no if it is an alias (`-latest`, no date or version), falls back to one when unset, or is the app release number. Also no if adapters or checkpoints are used but left out.

checks.check: The manifest is put in a fixed, documented order before hashing, so the same manifest always gives the same ID.
checks.verify: 1) Open the serialization step before hashing. 2) Check for a fixed order: sorted keys (`sort_keys=True`), sorted file lists, fixed encoding and line endings. 3) Check file lists are not taken straight from directory listing or map iteration order. 4) Answer no if any unsorted dict, map, or filesystem order reaches the hash.

checks.check: Secret values are not placed in the hashed manifest in a form that exposes them.
checks.verify: 1) List every value fed into the manifest or hash. 2) Check whether any are secrets: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, `.env` contents. 3) Answer no if a secret value is written in plain text to the stored manifest, or the whole environment is dumped into it.

findings.title: Trustworthy attribution
findings.requirement: Assign instance and tenant identity in the trusted execution layer. Don't accept labels the model supplies. Record the delegated subject — the user or system whose authority is being used — separately from the agent's identity. Test that the agent can't pose as another instance or tenant in requests or audit records. Test that trace context survives handoffs between async jobs. Treat trace IDs and caller-supplied labels only as a way to link records. They never prove identity or permission.

not_covered.problem: Agent sharing the launching user's identity
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded
Sub-agent authorized using an earlier actor's authority
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

checks.check: Tenant and instance identity are set by the harness or platform from verified context, never from model-produced text or tool arguments.
checks.verify: 1) Find every place tenant and instance IDs are set for tool calls and records. 2) Check each comes from verified context (token claims, session bound at launch). 3) Check tool JSON schemas the model fills for `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `instance_id`. 4) Answer no if any function uses the model's value, even if another function uses verified context.

checks.check: Tenant or instance labels in tool arguments or agent-controlled headers are rejected or overwritten with the verified values before they are used or logged.
checks.verify: 1) Find tool handlers and middleware that receive tool arguments and headers. 2) Check that tenant or instance fields in arguments, or headers like `X-Tenant-Id`, are rejected or overwritten with the verified value before use or logging. 3) Answer no if any handler uses or logs the supplied value, or detects a mismatch and continues.

checks.check: The delegated subject is recorded separately from the agent identity.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record schema and writer. 2) Look for a delegated-subject field (the user or system whose authority is used) separate from the agent principal field. 3) Answer no if only one identity is stored, the user overwrites the agent identity, or the field is never filled.

checks.check: When work is handed to an async job or queue, the trusted layer attaches the verified attribution and trace context, and the job uses them.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue producers and enqueue calls (Celery, SQS, Pub/Sub, Kafka, cron). 2) Check the trusted layer adds verified identity and trace context to the job. 3) Check the worker uses those values, not ones the agent wrote. 4) Answer no if workers start new traces without parent context or take tenant from agent-written job data.

checks.check: Authorization never treats trace IDs or caller-supplied labels as proof of identity or permission.
checks.verify: 1) Find authorization and permission-lookup code. 2) Check what each decision is keyed on. 3) Answer no if any check uses a trace ID, span ID, correlation ID, request label, or caller-supplied header as identity or to look up permissions.

findings.title: Operational lookup
findings.requirement: Start from one suspicious action. Find the team responsible, the current operator, the deployment manifest, and the live instance. Show that you can contain the right instance or agent type without cutting off the launching user's other access.

not_covered.problem: Stop doesn't halt running work or open tool streams within a set time
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

checks.check: Each audit record carries the agent-type-id and agent-instance-id, which resolve to a stored deployment manifest and a live instance.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record writer. 2) Check `agent.type.id` and `agent.instance.id` are written on every record. 3) Check the type ID can be looked up to a stored manifest (registry, manifest store, file keyed by hash). 4) Answer no if either field is missing or nothing stores manifests by that ID. Answer unknown if the lookup store is outside this repo.

checks.check: An ownership record in code or config maps each agent type to a responsible team and a current operator or on-call rotation.
checks.verify: 1) Look for CODEOWNERS, `catalog-info.yaml`, `.brace/deployment.yaml`, or another ownership file. 2) Check each agent type maps to a team and to a current operator or on-call rotation. 3) Answer no if an agent type has no owner, or owners exist only in prose with no link. Answer unknown if ownership lives in an outside catalog.

checks.check: A containment control can disable a single instance or a single agent type (for example revoke its principal or scale it to zero) without touching the launching user's credentials.
checks.verify: 1) Find stop and revoke controls: admin endpoints, CLIs, feature flags, scale-to-zero, per-instance token revocation. 2) Check their scope is one instance or one agent type. 3) Answer no if the only control is a global switch or revoking a shared or user credential. Answer unknown if containment is run by an outside platform.

findings.title: Parent and prompt provenance
findings.requirement: For every sub-agent, record its own type and instance IDs, a link to its parent, trace links, and the prompt the parent gave it. Trace a nested action back to that prompt. Protect sensitive prompt text with restricted storage and a clear redaction policy. Standard GenAI instrumentation records prompts only when you turn that on, so confirm it is on for this path.

not_covered.problem: Sub-agent given powers beyond its task
Children still running after the parent is stopped
No limit on how many sub-agents a run can start

checks.check: Each sub-agent gets its own type ID and instance ID, assigned by the harness when it is started.
checks.verify: 1) Find sub-agent spawn code (handoffs, subgraphs, subagents, A2A task creation). 2) Check the harness assigns the child a new `agent.instance.id` and a type ID at start. 3) Answer no if any spawn path reuses the parent's IDs, assigns none, or takes the IDs from the model's request.

checks.check: Each sub-agent's records include its direct parent's instance ID and a trace link to the parent.
checks.verify: 1) Open sub-agent spawn code and the child's record writer. 2) Look for a parent instance field (for example `agent.parent.instance_id`) and trace propagation (span parent, span link, `traceparent` in queued payloads). 3) Answer no if any spawn path, including remote or queued, starts a fresh trace or omits the parent ID.

checks.check: The prompt the parent passed to the child is captured on this path, with prompt capture switched on in config rather than left at the default off.
checks.verify: 1) Find where the parent's prompt to the child is recorded (for example `agent.parent.prompt`, or a hash plus stored text). 2) Check prompt content capture is turned on in config, for example a GenAI capture-content env var or SDK option. 3) Answer no if capture is left at its default off, or the setting falls back to false when unset.

checks.check: Captured prompt text is stored with restricted access and a redaction policy, and only an approved audit role can read it.
checks.verify: 1) Find where captured prompt text is stored (bucket, table, log index). 2) Check its IAM or ACL limits reads to an approved audit role. 3) Check a redaction policy is defined and applied. 4) Answer no if prompts go to general logs the whole team can read, or no redaction exists. Answer unknown if storage access is set outside this repo.

findings.title: Every model in the loop
findings.requirement: List all helper models, such as verifiers, judges, rerankers, and world models. Give each one an identity based on its available model version or digest, its prompt, and its configuration, and record which decisions it made. Show that a swapped, drifting, or failing checker counts as a failure of the control that depends on it.

not_covered.problem: Main agent model changing behind a fixed name unnoticed
Second-model review not tested against evasive behavior
Self-hosted model weights loaded without a signature or format check

checks.check: A model inventory in code or config lists every helper model the agent calls (verifiers, judges, rerankers, embedding models, world models).
checks.verify: 1) Search for every model call: provider SDK clients, model name strings, embedding, rerank, moderation, and judge calls. 2) Compare that list with the model inventory. 3) Answer no if any helper model called in code is missing from the inventory, or no inventory exists.

checks.check: Each helper model is identified by a pinned version or digest plus its prompt and configuration, not by an alias.
checks.verify: 1) For each helper model, find its model ID and follow env vars to the final value. 2) Check it is a pinned version or digest, and that its prompt and configuration are also recorded. 3) Answer no if any is an alias (`-latest`, undated name), falls back to one by default, or is hard-coded inline outside the inventory.

checks.check: Each helper model's decisions are logged with that model's identity.
checks.verify: 1) Open each helper or checker call site. 2) Check its decision is logged with that model's ID and version. 3) Answer no if decisions are logged without model identity, or logged only on the allow or success branch.

checks.check: A checker timeout, error, invalid output, or version mismatch makes the control that depends on it fail (block or escalate), not pass by default.
checks.verify: 1) Open each checker call site (judge, guardrail, moderation, verifier). 2) Read every `try/except`, `catch`, timeout, and parse-error branch. 3) Check each one blocks or escalates. 4) Answer no if any branch returns allow, skips the check, treats unparseable output as safe, or logs and continues. Also no if the returned model version is never compared with the expected one.

findings.title: Minimal tool surface
findings.requirement: List every built-in tool, MCP server, API, program, and file permission this agent type can use. Give a task-based reason for each. Enforce a role-based allowlist, and check that an unlisted tool can't be called. Don't base allow or approval decisions on hints a server gives about its own tools, such as "read-only." MCP treats those hints as untrusted unless you trust the server.

not_covered.problem: A tool call that skips the MCP gateway or reaches a tool server directly
A token or credential with too much access
Hidden instructions inside a tool's description or schema
A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Lookalike or duplicate tool names across servers

checks.check: Each agent role has one explicit allowlist of tool names, with no wildcard grants such as `*`, `mcp__*`, `Bash(*)`, or `bypassPermissions`.
checks.verify: 1) Find where each agent is built and tools are passed (`allowed_tools`, `tools=[`, `allowedTools`, `.mcp.json`, `settings.json`). 2) Check each role has one fixed list of names. 3) Answer no if any list holds `*`, `mcp__*`, `Bash(*)`, a pattern or regex, `bypassPermissions`, or is built from `list_tools()`, or if a second agent role or entry point has no list.

checks.check: Tools discovered from MCP servers are filtered against that allowlist before the model can see or call them.
checks.verify: 1) Find MCP discovery (`list_tools`, `session.list_tools`, `tools/list`, MCP client setup). 2) Trace the result to where it is handed to the model. 3) Confirm a filter keeps only names on the allowlist. 4) Answer no if any discovered tool reaches the model unfiltered, the filter is a denylist or prefix match (`startswith`, `mcp__server__`), or a refresh or reconnect path skips it.

checks.check: The dispatcher rejects a call to any tool name not on the allowlist, instead of looking it up dynamically.
checks.verify: 1) Find the dispatcher (search `tool_use`, `call_tool`, `dispatch`, `execute`, `getattr`, `registry[`). 2) Check it rejects names not on the allowlist with an error. 3) Answer no if it looks tools up with `getattr`, `globals()`, `eval`, or a registry holding more than the allowlist, falls back to calling the MCP server directly, or catches the unknown-tool error and continues.

checks.check: Allow and approval decisions never read server-supplied hints or descriptions such as `readOnlyHint` or 'read-only'.
checks.verify: 1) Search for `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `annotations`, `description`, and approval or auto-approve code. 2) Check whether any allow, skip-approval, or permission branch reads these. 3) Answer no if any allow or approval decision depends on a server hint or tool description text, including a default that auto-approves tools marked read-only.

checks.check: File access is limited to named directories, not the whole filesystem.
checks.verify: 1) Find file tools and mounts (`allowed_directories`, `cwd`, `open(`, `fs.`, `os.ReadFile`, container `volumes`, `mountPath`). 2) Check paths are resolved (`realpath`, `resolve`, `filepath.Clean`) then compared to named directories. 3) Answer no if access is unrestricted, `/` or home is mounted, the check is a string `startsWith`/prefix test without resolving `..` and symlinks, or a shell tool bypasses it.

findings.title: Least-privilege access
findings.requirement: Limit credentials to named operations and resources, including tenant boundaries. Test that an allowed read works. Test that an out-of-scope write, an admin action, and a request for another tenant's data all fail. Limit each token to its intended audience, so other services reject it. Remove wildcard permissions and permissions inherited from people.

not_covered.problem: A retrieval search or cache not filtered by the requesting tenant or user
Long-lived or static secrets that never expire or rotate
Revocation delay from cached or self-contained tokens
A sub-agent getting powers beyond its task, or a parent escalating through a peer
Memory readable across tenants or tasks

checks.check: The agent's IAM policy or role names specific actions and resources, with no `*` action or resource and no owner, editor, or cluster-admin role.
checks.verify: 1) Find IAM and RBAC files (`*.tf`, `iam*.json`, `Role`, `ClusterRoleBinding`, `RoleBinding`, CloudFormation). 2) Find the policy attached to the agent's identity. 3) Answer no if any `Action` or `Resource` is `*` or a service wildcard (`s3:*`), or it binds `roles/owner`, `roles/editor`, `cluster-admin`, or AdministratorAccess. Answer unknown if the agent's IAM is not in this repo.

checks.check: Tenant scope is enforced in the credential or the data layer (token claim, row-level security, or per-tenant account), not by the prompt or by code the model's output controls.
checks.verify: 1) Find how queries and API calls pick a tenant (search `tenant`, `org_id`, row-level security, `CREATE POLICY`, per-tenant credentials). 2) Trace where the tenant value comes from. 3) Answer no if one shared login or key reaches all tenants and the tenant ID comes from the prompt, a tool argument the model fills, or app code filtering after the query.

checks.check: Tokens are issued with a set audience, and receiving services reject tokens whose audience does not match.
checks.verify: 1) Find token requests (`audience`, `aud`, `resource`, `scope`, token client setup). 2) Find token validation in receiving services (`verify`, `jwt.decode`, middleware). 3) Answer no if tokens are requested without an audience, validation skips `aud` (`verify_aud=False`, no audience option), or accepts a list or wildcard. Answer unknown if receiving services are outside this repo.

checks.check: The agent uses its own service identity, not a human user's token, a copied session, or an admin key.
checks.verify: 1) Find where the agent loads credentials (env vars, `credentials`, `token`, `Authorization`, service account settings). 2) Check they belong to a service or workload identity for the agent. 3) Answer no if it uses a user's OAuth or session token, a personal access token, an admin or root key, or forwards the calling user's token to tools.

findings.title: Credential lifetime and handling
findings.requirement: Issue short-lived credentials from a managed identity or secrets service. Keep long-lived secrets out of prompts, images, and checked-in config. Where the service supports it, bind tokens to their holder (mTLS, DPoP, or workload proof tokens). Then a copied token won't work from another machine. Don't use fixed API keys when short-lived or federated credentials are available. Show that credentials expire and rotate, and explain why you chose their lifetime.

not_covered.problem: A credential scoped to more operations, resources, or tenants than needed
No way to cut off the agent's access without cutting off the user
Secrets showing up in tool output, responses, or normal logs
Container image not pinned by digest or signature-checked

checks.check: Credentials are fetched at run time from a managed identity or secrets service, not fixed API keys, where short-lived or federated credentials are available.
checks.verify: 1) Find credential setup (`AssumeRole`, IRSA, Workload Identity, Managed Identity, Vault, `os.environ`, `process.env`). 2) Check each credential is fetched at run time. 3) Answer no if a fixed key (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `API_KEY` in a Secret or env) is used for a service that offers federated or short-lived credentials, or code falls back to a static key when the managed source fails.

checks.check: Credential lifetime and rotation are set in config to bounded values.
checks.verify: 1) Search for lifetime and rotation settings (`DurationSeconds`, `ttl`, `expires_in`, `max_ttl`, rotation job or policy). 2) Check each credential the agent uses has a bounded value. 3) Answer no if any credential has no expiry, no rotation, or an unbounded or very long value. Answer unknown if lifetimes are set in an identity provider outside this repo.

checks.check: No long-lived secrets appear in prompts, Dockerfiles or image layers, or checked-in config.
checks.verify: 1) Search prompt templates, Dockerfiles (`ENV`, `ARG`, `COPY .env`), `.env*`, `*.yaml`, `*.tfvars`, `.mcp.json` `env` blocks for key-like literals (`sk-`, `AKIA`, `token:`, `password:`). 2) Check prompt-building code for env values inserted into messages. 3) Answer no if any real secret is checked in, baked into an image, or placed in a prompt; `.gitignore` listing a file does not count if it is committed.

checks.check: Where the service supports it, tokens are bound to their holder with mTLS, DPoP, or workload proof tokens.
checks.verify: 1) Find token and client setup for each service (`mTLS`, `client_cert`, `DPoP`, `cert-bound`, SPIFFE). 2) Check whether the service supports holder binding. 3) Answer no if a supporting service uses plain bearer tokens. Answer unknown if support depends on a provider outside this repo and nothing states it.

findings.title: Independent revocation
findings.requirement: Show that an operator can cut off this agent's access without cutting off the user who launched it. The agent must not need to cooperate. Set and measure the longest time before the cutoff takes effect. Count cached tokens, self-contained tokens, and open sessions. A trusted enforcement point must block later calls within a time limit that fits the potential harm. Revoking only the refresh token is not enough. If tokens live longer than that limit, push the revocation to each service (for example, with OpenID CAEP session-revoked events) or make the tokens shorter-lived.

not_covered.problem: A kill switch that doesn't stop running work or open tool streams
Sub-agents or remote workers still acting after the parent is stopped
Static API keys used where short-lived credentials are available
No way to trace a suspicious action to its team, operator, and live instance

checks.check: A revocation control disables the agent's own identity or credentials without disabling the user who launched it.
checks.verify: 1) Find a disable or revoke path (script, runbook, IdP config, `disable`, `revoke`, deny list). 2) Check it targets the agent's own identity or credential. 3) Answer no if the agent uses the user's token, so revocation disables the user too, or no revoke path exists. Answer unknown if revocation lives only in an identity provider outside this repo.

checks.check: Revocation is applied at a trusted enforcement point (identity provider, gateway, or target service) and does not need the agent's cooperation.
checks.verify: 1) Find where revocation is checked (gateway, auth middleware, IdP, introspection, deny list lookup). 2) Check it runs outside the agent process. 3) Answer no if revocation sends a message or signal to the agent and relies on it to drop credentials, or the check runs inside agent code.

checks.check: Later calls are blocked even with cached tokens, self-contained tokens, and open sessions: token lifetime is shorter than the revocation limit, or revocation is pushed to each service (for example CAEP) or checked on every call.
checks.verify: 1) Find access-token lifetimes and how services validate tokens (signature only vs `introspect`, deny list, CAEP). 2) Compare lifetime with the stated revocation limit. 3) Answer no if self-contained JWTs outlive the limit and are checked by signature only, cached tokens or open sessions skip the check, or no limit is stated. Answer unknown if validation lives outside this repo.

checks.check: Revocation covers access tokens and open sessions, not only the refresh token.
checks.verify: 1) Find the revoke code or runbook. 2) List what it revokes: refresh token, access tokens, sessions, streams. 3) Answer no if it only revokes the refresh token or deletes stored credentials while issued access tokens and open sessions stay valid.

findings.title: Destructive-action interception
findings.requirement: List the high-impact operations. These include deletes, destructive database updates, force-pushes, tearing down infrastructure, payment changes, and sending anything outside. Block them by default in the execution path. Allow one only when a reviewer or system with higher authority approves that specific action. When the action runs, authorize its operation, target, and arguments, and block it if they aren't allowed. A list of blocked words or command names is not enough. Test other tools and raw API or shell paths that could do the same thing. Treat deleting audit records, or changing how long they are kept, as high-impact too. That includes asking a more powerful tool or peer to do it. Some agents can do all three of these in one context: read untrusted input, reach sensitive data or systems, and change things or talk to the outside. For those agents, treat every consequential action as high-impact. The exception is a design that stops untrusted content from picking the tool, destination, or arguments. Examples are plan-then-execute, a two-model pattern, or capability tracking such as CaMeL. Record which of the three each agent type has.

not_covered.problem: Denied actions not recorded in the audit trail
Approvals that can be replayed, reused in parallel, or used after expiry
Outside effects left unreconciled after the agent is stopped
A chain of individually allowed actions that adds up to data theft
Tool output not labelled or kept apart from trusted instructions

checks.check: High-impact operations are listed in code or config and blocked by default, including deletes, destructive updates, force-pushes, infrastructure teardown, payment changes, outbound sends, and deleting audit records or changing their retention.
checks.verify: 1) Search code and config for a list of high-impact operations (deny/approval policy, OPA/Rego, Cedar, hook config). 2) Check it covers deletes, destructive updates, force-push, teardown, payments, outbound sends, audit deletion or retention changes. 3) Answer no if no list exists, any category is missing with a tool that can do it, or unlisted operations default to `allow`.

checks.check: The gate runs in the execution path when the call runs and checks the operation, the target, and the arguments, not only a tool name, command name, or blocklist of words.
checks.verify: 1) Find where tool calls execute (`tool_use`, `call_tool`, `execute`, `can_use_tool`, `PreToolUse`). 2) Find the gate that runs before the side effect and see what it inspects. 3) Answer no if it checks only the tool or command name, matches words (`'rm' in cmd`, `DROP`), runs after the call, lives only in the prompt, or sits in a `try`/`catch` that continues on error. 4) For each value that lets an action skip approval (an internal recipient, a small amount, a safe path), read the comparison itself: answer no if a domain, host, or path is matched by suffix, prefix, or substring without an anchor, so `endswith('example.com')` also passes `evil-example.com`.

checks.check: The same gate covers every path that can do the operation, including raw shell, HTTP or API clients, other tools, and requests to a more powerful tool or peer agent.
checks.verify: 1) Open the tool registry or config and write every tool the model can call into your note, by name, including MCP servers and sub-agents. 2) For each, say whether it can do a gated operation, including through a page it controls: a browser click or form fill in a logged-in session can buy, send, or delete. 3) Trace each such tool to the gate. 4) Answer no if any alias, raw shell or HTTP tool, browser action, second dispatch path, peer agent, or more powerful MCP tool can do the operation without passing the same gate.

checks.check: A blocked operation runs only after approval from a person or system with higher authority than the agent; a prompt, comment, or model instruction is never the enforcement.
checks.verify: 1) Find what happens when the gate blocks (approval request, `interrupt()`, `needs_approval`, webhook to reviewer). 2) Check who approves. 3) Answer no if the model, the agent itself, or a prompt instruction can approve, if approval is auto-granted (`bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits`, auto-approve flag, `yes` default), or if a timeout proceeds.

checks.check: For an agent that reads untrusted input, reaches sensitive data or systems, and acts outside, every consequential action is gated, unless code shows untrusted content cannot pick the tool, destination, or arguments (for example plan-then-execute or capability tracking).
checks.verify: 1) Check whether the agent reads untrusted content (web, email, files, tool output), reaches sensitive data, and can act outside. 2) If all three, list consequential actions and check each is gated. 3) Answer no if any is ungated and untrusted content can choose its tool, destination, or arguments with no plan-then-execute or capability tracking in code. Answer yes if the three are not combined.

findings.title: Approval integrity
findings.requirement: Tie each approval to the agent instance that asked, and to the exact operation, target, arguments, and scope. Record who approved it and when it expires. Show the reviewer what the action will do. Make approvals single-use, or set clear limits on a broader grant. When the action runs, check permissions and the relevant resource state again. Record each use of an approval in one step, so parallel calls can't go past the grant. Test changed arguments, a different agent instance, expired approvals, replay, parallel reuse, and approvers without authority. If the approval service fails, the action must not quietly go ahead.

not_covered.problem: A high-impact action that never asks for approval at all
A parent gaining a denied power by asking a stronger peer
Harness or approval code changed in production without review

checks.check: Each approval record is bound to the requesting agent instance and to the exact operation, target, arguments, and scope, and records the approver and an expiry time.
checks.verify: 1) Find the approval data model (schema, class, table, `approval`). 2) List its fields. 3) Answer no if it lacks any of agent instance ID, operation, target, exact arguments or hash, scope, approver, and expiry, or if approval is a boolean like `approved=True`.

checks.check: When the action runs, the gate rejects it if the instance, operation, target, or arguments differ from the approval, or if the approval has expired.
checks.verify: 1) Find where an approved action executes. 2) Check the code compares instance, operation, target, and arguments (or hash) against the stored approval and checks expiry at that moment. 3) Answer no if approval is checked only when requested, any field is not compared, arguments are re-read from the model after the check, or expiry is never checked.

checks.check: Each use of an approval is recorded in one atomic step (single-use or a bounded counter), so replays and parallel calls cannot go past the grant.
checks.verify: 1) Find where an approval is used or marked consumed. 2) Check it is one atomic step: transaction with lock, compare-and-set, unique constraint, or atomic decrement. 3) Answer no if it reads then writes separately, never marks use, or keeps the count in process memory that parallel workers do not share.

checks.check: The gate checks that the approver has authority for this action, and rechecks permissions and the relevant resource state when the action runs.
checks.verify: 1) Find approver checks (role list, `can_approve`, authority mapping). 2) Find rechecks of permissions and resource state at execution. 3) Answer no if any logged-in user can approve, the approver is not checked against the action, or permissions and resource state are not rechecked when the action runs.

checks.check: If the approval service errors or cannot be reached, the action is denied.
checks.verify: 1) Find calls to the approval service. 2) Read their error, timeout, and exception handling. 3) Answer no if a `try`/`except` or `catch` logs and proceeds, the default on error or timeout is allow, or a missing response is treated as approved.

findings.title: Hard execution budgets
findings.requirement: Enforce limits outside the model on loop count, run time, tokens, cost, tool-call rate, and how many sub-agents it can start. Also set spend and rate quotas per user or service, per tenant, and across the whole fleet. That way, many small runs can't use up shared capacity. Hit each limit in a test, and record how the run stops or escalates.

not_covered.problem: Budget or cross-agent abuse alerts not reaching the team that can act
Unusual fan-out or resource use going undetected
Context size not logged for each action decision

checks.check: Limits on loop count, run time, tokens, cost, tool-call rate, and number of sub-agents started are set in code or config.
checks.verify: 1) Search for `max_turns`, `recursion_limit`, `max_iterations`, `timeout`, `max_tokens`, cost or budget caps, rate limits, sub-agent caps. 2) Check each of the six limits has a value. 3) Answer no if any is missing, set to unlimited (`None`, `0`, `-1`, `inf`), or the loop is `while True` with no cap.

checks.check: The harness or a gateway outside the model enforces each limit and stops or escalates the run when it is hit; the model cannot raise, reset, or skip them.
checks.verify: 1) For each limit, find the code that enforces it and what happens when hit. 2) Check it runs in the harness or gateway. 3) Answer no if a limit is only in the prompt, can be changed by a tool argument or model output, is caught and the run continues, or hitting it has no stop or escalation.

checks.check: Budgets apply to nested sub-agents, so their usage counts against the limits.
checks.verify: 1) Find sub-agent spawning (`spawn`, `Task`, `handoff`, `create_agent`). 2) Check child runs share or deduct from the parent budget and depth is capped. 3) Answer no if each child gets a fresh budget, nested spawns are uncounted, or depth and count are unlimited.

checks.check: Spend and rate quotas also apply per user or service, per tenant, and across the fleet, counted across runs, not only within one run.
checks.verify: 1) Search gateway, LLM proxy (LiteLLM budgets), and provider config for per-user, per-tenant, and fleet quotas. 2) Check counts persist across runs (shared store, not process memory). 3) Answer no if only per-run limits exist. Answer unknown if quotas would live in a provider console or gateway outside this repo.

findings.title: Environment isolation
findings.requirement: Write down every system and data store the agent can reach. Test that it has no path to unapproved production resources, admin systems, host services, or other tenants. Enforce this in the infrastructure, not only in the prompt. For each allowed connection, also check input and response validation under R01–R02, including API responses and messages from connected services. Being allowed on the network does not make their content trusted.

not_covered.problem: Outbound traffic to unapproved internet destinations
Container running as root or shipping a shell it doesn't need
Content from an allowed service trusted without validation
Agent reaching an approved MCP server directly instead of through the gateway

checks.check: Network policy or security groups default-deny and allow only the listed systems and data stores the agent needs.
checks.verify: 1) Find NetworkPolicy, security groups, firewall rules, docker-compose networks. 2) Check for a default deny and named allowed peers. 3) Answer no if the agent's namespace has no policy, rules allow all, `0.0.0.0/0` or a broad CIDR is allowed, or allowed peers go beyond the listed systems. Answer unknown if network config lives outside this repo.

checks.check: No route, mount, or credential gives the runtime a path to unapproved production resources, admin systems, host services, or other tenants. Egress to 0.0.0.0/0 or another broad range, even only on ports 80 and 443, is such a route: it reaches cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) and internal services unless they are explicitly blocked.
checks.verify: 1) List routes, mounts, and credentials in the agent's runtime (egress rules, volumes, env secrets, `hostNetwork`, `docker.sock`). 2) Check each reaches only approved systems. 3) Answer no if egress allows `0.0.0.0/0` or a broad range on any port without blocking 169.254.169.254, if host services or the Docker socket are reachable, or credentials reach production admin or other tenants.

checks.check: Isolation is enforced in infrastructure config, not by the prompt or by agent code the model can influence.
checks.verify: 1) Find where isolation is defined. 2) Check it is in infrastructure (NetworkPolicy, VPC, IAM, separate namespace or account). 3) Answer no if it relies on prompt text or agent code (URL checks, host lists in the harness) that the model's output can steer, with no infrastructure rule behind it.

findings.title: Egress allowlist
findings.requirement: Allow only the outside destinations the task needs. Test a blocked destination and ways around the block, such as going straight past a proxy or gateway. Cover redirects, DNS changes and rebinding, IPv4 and IPv6, and cloud metadata or loopback addresses where they apply. An allowed domain can still host an attacker's account or receive leaked data. So also limit which resources and tenants the agent can reach, and what data it can send. Record each block and confirm the right operator hears about it.

not_covered.problem: Data leaking through client-side Markdown images or link previews
Network path to internal production or admin systems
A loosened egress rule in the running setup raising no alert

checks.check: Outbound traffic is default-deny, with a destination allowlist enforced at a proxy, gateway, or network policy.
checks.verify: 1) Find egress rules (NetworkPolicy egress, Cilium FQDN, proxy ACLs, cloud firewall). 2) Check outbound is default deny with a destination allowlist. 3) Answer no if egress allows `0.0.0.0/0` or broad CIDRs, no egress rules exist, or the allowlist is only in app code the agent runs. Answer unknown if egress is set outside this repo.

checks.check: Network policy blocks direct routes around the proxy or gateway, for both IPv4 and IPv6.
checks.verify: 1) Check whether the proxy is enforced by network policy or only by `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` env. 2) Check IPv6 egress rules. 3) Answer no if pods can reach the internet except via the proxy, the proxy is only an env var, `NO_PROXY` is broad, or IPv6 is not restricted.

checks.check: Redirect targets and resolved IP addresses are checked against the allowlist, and cloud metadata and loopback addresses are blocked.
checks.verify: 1) Find fetch and HTTP client code (`requests`, `fetch`, `http.Client`, `follow_redirects`, `allow_redirects`). 2) Check each redirect hop and resolved IP is checked. 3) Answer no if redirects are followed unchecked, the check uses the hostname but not the resolved IP, or 169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254, or 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 are not blocked.

checks.check: Allowed destinations are limited by resource, tenant, or path where needed, not only by domain.
checks.verify: 1) List allowed destinations that are shared services (S3, GitHub, storage, paste sites). 2) Check rules limit bucket, account, repo, tenant, or path. 3) Answer no if a shared service is allowed by domain or wildcard (`*.s3.amazonaws.com`) alone, or path checks use string prefix without normalising.

checks.check: Each blocked request is logged and routed as an alert to a named operator.
checks.verify: 1) Find where blocked requests are logged (proxy deny log, policy audit, app code). 2) Find the alert route to a named operator. 3) Answer no if blocks are not logged, only allowed requests are logged, or no alert route names an operator. Answer unknown if alerting lives outside this repo.

findings.title: Pinned, verified image
findings.requirement: Pin the container by digest. Before it runs, check its digest and signature against an approved signing key, or an approved certificate identity and issuer. Keep its build provenance (the record of how it was built) and its list of dependencies. Check provenance fields such as the builder, source repository, build type, and the parameters set from outside the build (SLSA `externalParameters`) against what you expect. Keep the verifier patched. Cosign versions before 2.6.2 and 3.0.4 could accept a bundle whose transparency-log entry didn't match the artifact. Confirm that the admission check covers production namespaces and is set to enforce, not just audit. Show that an unapproved or changed image is rejected.

not_covered.problem: Tool or MCP server package not vetted or pinned
Model weights or adapters loaded without a signature or format check
Image runs as root or includes a shell or package manager
Secrets baked into the image

checks.check: Production manifests reference images by digest (`@sha256:`), not by tag alone.
checks.verify: 1) Find every `image:` field in manifests, Helm values, compose, and Terraform. 2) Check each uses `@sha256:`. 3) Answer no if any production image uses only a tag (`:latest`, `:v1`), or a template defaults to a tag when the digest value is empty.

checks.check: An admission policy verifies the signature against a pinned key, or a pinned certificate identity and issuer, with no wildcard identity or issuer.
checks.verify: 1) Find admission policies (Kyverno `verifyImages`, `ClusterImagePolicy`, Gatekeeper). 2) Check the key or certificate identity and issuer are pinned. 3) Answer no if identity or issuer uses `.*` or wildcard regex, issuer is unset, or no admission policy exists. Answer unknown if admission config is outside this repo.

checks.check: The policy checks provenance fields: builder, source repository, build type, and external parameters.
checks.verify: 1) In the admission policy, find attestation or provenance conditions. 2) Check builder ID, source repository, build type, and `externalParameters` are each compared to expected values. 3) Answer no if any is missing, provenance is only generated in CI but not verified, or conditions use wildcards.

checks.check: The policy is in enforce mode, covers production namespaces, and denies images that match no policy.
checks.verify: 1) Read the policy mode and scope (`validationFailureAction`, `failureAction`, `mode`, namespace selectors, exclusions). 2) Check for a no-match deny. 3) Answer no if mode is `Audit` or `warn`, production namespaces are excluded or unmatched, `failurePolicy: Ignore`, or images matching no policy are allowed.

checks.check: The pinned Cosign or verifier version is at least 2.6.2 (2.x) or 3.0.4 (3.x).
checks.verify: 1) Find Cosign or verifier versions in CI workflows (`cosign-installer`, `cosign-release`), Dockerfiles, and policy-controller charts. 2) Compare to 2.6.2 (2.x) and 3.0.4 (3.x). 3) Answer no if any pin is lower or uses `latest` or no version. Answer unknown if no verifier is in this repo.

findings.title: Minimal, isolated runtime
findings.requirement: Remove shells, downloaders, package managers, mounts, and privileges the agent doesn't need. As a container baseline, meet the Kubernetes Pod Security Standards "restricted" profile or the same controls elsewhere. That means non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, and a seccomp profile set. Where supported, also use a read-only root filesystem and user namespaces; the restricted profile doesn't require those two. For running untrusted code, use a sandbox that fits the threat, such as a microVM or a user-space kernel. Ordinary containers share the host's kernel. For managed runtimes, record the provider's isolation evidence and what you can't see. Test that host access is blocked. A blocked probe does not prove the sandbox resists every escape.

not_covered.problem: Container image not pinned by digest or signature-checked
Outbound traffic to unapproved internet destinations
Network path to admin systems or other tenants' resources

checks.check: Container settings set non-root, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, and a seccomp profile, matching Pod Security 'restricted' or the same controls.
checks.verify: 1) Find pod `securityContext` and container `securityContext`, plus namespace labels. 2) Check `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `capabilities.drop: [ALL]`, `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`. 3) Answer no if any is missing on any container (including init and sidecars), set the wrong way, or overridden per container, or the Dockerfile runs as root with no override.

checks.check: The final image has no shell, downloader, or package manager the agent does not need.
checks.verify: 1) Read the final stage of each Dockerfile (after the last `FROM`). 2) Check base image and installs for `bash`, `sh`, `curl`, `wget`, `apt`, `apk`, `pip`, `npm`. 3) Answer no if the final image has any the agent does not need, or the final stage is a full OS image (ubuntu, debian, python) not distroless or scratch.

checks.check: There is no privileged mode, hostPath or Docker socket mount, or host network or PID namespace.
checks.verify: 1) Search manifests and compose for `privileged`, `hostPath`, `docker.sock`, `hostNetwork`, `hostPID`, `hostIPC`, `network_mode: host`, `pid: host`. 2) Answer no if any appears on the agent's workloads, including sidecars and init containers.

checks.check: If the agent runs untrusted or model-written code, that code runs in a separate sandbox such as gVisor, Kata, or a microVM, not in the agent's own container.
checks.verify: 1) Find code execution tools (`subprocess`, `exec`, `eval`, `child_process`, `os/exec`, code interpreter). 2) Check where that code runs (`runtimeClassName: gvisor`, Kata, Firecracker, remote sandbox API). 3) Answer no if model-written or untrusted code runs in the agent's own process or container, or the sandbox call falls back to local execution on error. Answer yes if no such code runs.

findings.title: Reviewed harness and instructions
findings.requirement: Version and review the harness, system prompt, and rules files before release. Allow production changes only through a release process that records who made them. Protect source branches from history rewrites, so the reviewed diff stays available. Link the deployed versions to the approved review. Complete the full configuration checks in section C.

not_covered.problem: Running config drifting from the approved baseline
Model or dependency change promoted without review and re-testing
A tool server changing its description or schema after approval
Release candidate not re-tested against attack cases

checks.check: The harness, system prompt, and rules files are in version control and loaded from the reviewed build, not fetched at run time from a database, URL, or feature flag.
checks.verify: 1) Find where the system prompt and rules are loaded (`system_prompt`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `prompts/`). 2) Check they come from files in the repo or build. 3) Answer no if any part is fetched at run time from a database, URL, feature flag, or env var with no recorded version, or a remote source overrides the file when available.

checks.check: CODEOWNERS or required-review rules cover the prompt, rules, and harness files.
checks.verify: 1) Read `CODEOWNERS` and review rules (`.github/`, rulesets, branch protection IaC). 2) Check patterns match prompt, rules, and harness paths. 3) Answer no if those paths are uncovered, the pattern misses them (wrong glob, case), or no CODEOWNERS exists. Answer unknown if required reviews are set only in repo settings outside the code.

checks.check: Production deploys run only from CI on the reviewed branch and record the commit, tag, or digest deployed.
checks.verify: 1) Read deploy workflows and scripts. 2) Check deploy triggers only on the reviewed branch and records commit, tag, or digest. 3) Answer no if `workflow_dispatch` or a script deploys any branch or local build, deploy scripts accept manual laptop pushes, or no version is recorded. Answer unknown if deploy is outside this repo.

checks.check: Branch protection config blocks force-pushes and history rewrites on the source branch.
checks.verify: 1) Search for branch protection IaC (`github_branch_protection`, rulesets JSON). 2) Check force-push and deletion are blocked on the source branch. 3) Answer no if `allow_force_pushes: true` or bypass is open to the agent's identity. Answer unknown if protection is set only in repo settings and not in code.

findings.title: Complete release manifest
findings.requirement: Write a release manifest: a list of everything that makes up this release. Include the container, harness, system prompt, rules files, model, built-in tools, MCP servers, permission scopes, memory and retrieval settings, identity bindings, network rules, and execution budgets. Include security-policy versions. Add a separate model record for every model: the main agent model, sub-agent models, and helper models such as embedding models and rerankers. For each, record the provider, model ID, exact version or checkpoint, and any adapter or fine-tune version. For training or fine-tuning you run yourself, also record the training job ID, base-model version, training code and config version, dataset version, and the digest of the output. The agent app's release number alone is not enough. Use the [model provenance fields](CHECKLIST-VERIFICATION.md#model-provenance-fields) to separate recorded versions from details a provider doesn't share. Check each model ID you request against the provider's versioning docs. Mark it as a pinned snapshot or as an alias that can change, and record which doc you used and its date. Naming rules differ by provider and model generation. Name each artifact's owner and a reference that can't change, where one exists. A machine-readable format, such as CycloneDX ML-BOM or the SPDX 3.0 AI and Dataset profiles, lets tools check the manifest.

not_covered.problem: Running setup not checked against the approved manifest
Manifest changes made without a reviewed diff and named author
Running config drifting from the approved baseline unnoticed
Agent-type-id not computed as a hash of its identity inputs

checks.check: A release manifest file lists the container, harness, system prompt, rules files, model, built-in tools, MCP servers, permission scopes, memory and retrieval settings, identity bindings, network rules, execution budgets, and security-policy versions.
checks.verify: 1) Find the release manifest (`.brace/manifest.yaml`, release manifest, ML-BOM). 2) Check each category: container, harness, system prompt, rules files, model, built-in tools, MCP servers, permission scopes, memory and retrieval, identity bindings, network rules, budgets, security-policy versions. 3) Compare with what config sets up (`*.mcp.json`, NetworkPolicy). 4) Answer no if any category is missing or configured items are left out.

checks.check: The manifest has a separate model record for every model (main, sub-agent, and helper models such as embedding models and rerankers), each with provider, model ID, exact version or checkpoint, and adapter or fine-tune version.
checks.verify: 1) Search code for every model used: main, sub-agent, embedding, reranker, judge. 2) Check the manifest has a separate record for each. 3) Check each record has provider, model ID, exact version or checkpoint, and adapter or fine-tune version. 4) Answer no if any model in code has no record, or a record is missing a field.

checks.check: Each requested model ID is labeled as a pinned snapshot or a changeable alias, with the provider doc and date used.
checks.verify: 1) Open each model record in the manifest. 2) Check it has a pinned-or-alias label, the provider doc used, and a date. 3) Answer no if any record lacks one of these, or labels an undated or `-latest` name as pinned.

checks.check: Each artifact has a named owner and a reference that can't change (digest or commit) where one exists, not a mutable tag or the app's release number.
checks.verify: 1) For each manifest artifact, check for a named owner. 2) Check its reference is a digest (`sha256:`) or commit SHA where one exists. 3) Answer no if any artifact has no owner, or uses a mutable tag (`:latest`, branch name) or the app release number where a digest or commit was available.

checks.check: For training the team runs itself, the manifest records the training job ID, base-model version, training code and config version, dataset version, and output digest.
checks.verify: 1) Search for training or fine-tuning code (training jobs, `Trainer`, fine-tune API calls, pipeline configs). 2) If found, check the manifest records job ID, base-model version, training code and config version, dataset version, and output digest. 3) Answer no if training runs here and any field is missing. Answer unknown if training may run in another repo.

findings.title: Review security-relevant changes
findings.requirement: Require diffs with a named author, plus review, for changes to the manifest and its policies. Show who is allowed to change production config. Record emergency changes with an owner, a reason, an end date, and a follow-up review.

not_covered.problem: Running config drifting from the approved baseline unnoticed
Release candidate not re-tested against attack cases
No tested rollback to an approved setup

checks.check: The manifest, prompts, tool config, and policy files live in version control, and merges require review by someone other than the named author.
checks.verify: 1) Check the manifest, prompts, tool config, and policy files are tracked in git, not loaded at runtime from an untracked path or remote URL. 2) Look for branch protection or ruleset config requiring approving review, and CODEOWNERS covering those paths. 3) Answer no if any of these files is untracked or not covered. Answer unknown if review rules are set only in the hosting service.

checks.check: Only named roles in config (CODEOWNERS, IAM, or protected CI environments) can change production configuration.
checks.verify: 1) Open CODEOWNERS, IAM policies, and CI environment config (protected `environment:` entries). 2) Check production config paths and deploy jobs are limited to named roles. 3) Answer no if a catch-all `*` owner, a broad group, or the agent's own credentials can change production config, or a deploy job skips the protected environment.

checks.check: An emergency change path exists that records an owner, a reason, an end date, and a follow-up review.
checks.verify: 1) Search for an emergency or break-glass path (runbook, workflow, CLI). 2) Check it records owner, reason, end date, and follow-up review. 3) Answer no if any of the four is missing, or the path bypasses review with no record. Answer unknown if the procedure lives outside this repo.

findings.title: Match release identity to running state
findings.requirement: Freeze the artifacts that define identity for each release. Check the running setup against the approved manifest, and emit the matching agent-type-id. Include the digest and signature of weights and adapters you host yourself. Test that a changed prompt, model, weights file, or tool setup can't keep showing the old approved identity without being caught.

not_covered.problem: Manifest missing helper models, budgets, or other components
Hosted model changing behind a fixed name
Agent-type-id not computed as a hash of its identity inputs
Container image not signature-checked at admission

checks.check: Identity-defining artifacts are referenced in deployment config by digest or a version that can't change, not by mutable tags.
checks.verify: 1) Open deployment config: Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Terraform, compose files. 2) Check images use `@sha256:` and prompts, models, and weights use fixed versions. 3) Follow variables and defaults to the final value. 4) Answer no if any reference is a tag like `:latest`, a branch, a model alias, or a default that falls back to one.

checks.check: A process outside the agent observes the running artifacts (image digest, prompt, model, tool setup) and compares them with the approved manifest, rather than trusting what the agent reports.
checks.verify: 1) Find a process outside the agent (admission controller, CI check, sidecar, scheduled job) that reads running artifacts. 2) Check it observes image digest, prompt, model, and tool setup itself and compares each with the approved manifest. 3) Answer no if it trusts values the agent reports, or compares a value with itself. Answer unknown if it would run in a platform outside this repo.

checks.check: The emitted agent-type-id is computed from the observed running artifacts, so a changed prompt, model, weights file, or tool setup produces a different ID instead of the approved one.
checks.verify: 1) Find where the emitted `agent.type.id` comes from. 2) Check it is computed from the observed running artifacts at start or deploy. 3) Answer no if it is a constant, an env var or config value set at build, or copied from the approved manifest, so a changed prompt, model, weights file, or tool setup would still emit the approved ID.

checks.check: Self-hosted weights and adapters are checked by digest and signature at load or deploy.
checks.verify: 1) Find where self-hosted weights and adapters are loaded or deployed (`from_pretrained`, `torch.load`, `safetensors`, download steps). 2) Check a digest compare and a signature check run before use. 3) Answer no if either is missing, wrapped in `try/except` that continues, or a second load path skips it. If only hosted models are used, answer yes citing the config that shows that.

checks.check: A mismatch blocks or quarantines the deployment, not only logs it.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code that handles a manifest or digest mismatch. 2) Check it blocks or quarantines: non-zero exit, admission deny, refusal to start, scale to zero. 3) Answer no if the mismatch branch only logs, warns, or emits a metric and continues, or an error in the check lets deployment proceed.

findings.title: Detect drift per agent
findings.requirement: Compare running images, harness settings, prompts, MCP server lists, permissions, network policies, and self-hosted model weights against their approved baseline. Simulate a prompt edit, an added tool, and a looser egress rule. Check that each one raises an alert and gets the documented response — block, quarantine, or rollback — within a set time.

not_covered.problem: Hosted model changing behind a fixed name
A tool server changing its description or schema after approval
Who may change production config, and emergency change records
Manifest missing components that define the release

checks.check: A drift check compares running images, harness settings, prompts, MCP server lists, permissions, network policies, and self-hosted model weights against the approved baseline, with each of these covered.
checks.verify: 1) Find the drift check job or tool. 2) List what it compares: images, harness settings, prompts, MCP server lists, permissions, network policies, self-hosted weights. 3) Check each is compared with the approved baseline, not with the live state itself. 4) Answer no if any category is missing or excluded. Answer unknown if drift detection runs in an outside platform.

checks.check: The drift check runs per agent deployment, on a schedule or on change events.
checks.verify: 1) Find what triggers the drift check: cron or CI schedule, admission webhook, or change events. 2) Check it runs for each agent deployment, not once for the fleet or only by hand. 3) Answer no if it is manual-only or covers only some deployments. Answer unknown if scheduling is set outside this repo.

checks.check: Detected drift triggers an alert and a set response (block, quarantine, or rollback) defined in config, with a time limit.
checks.verify: 1) Open the drift check's result handling. 2) Check drift raises an alert and triggers a response set in config: block, quarantine, or rollback. 3) Check a time limit is set. 4) Answer no if drift only logs, the response or time limit is missing, or a check error is treated as no drift.

findings.title: Control dependency, model, and training changes
findings.requirement: Pin dependency versions. Where supported, also pin each model's base version, checkpoint or weights, and fine-tune or adapter version. Before promotion, link any changed training run, dataset, or training code or config to the model it produced and to its test results. Record the model version actually served, when the runtime or provider shares it, separately from the name you requested. Before loading weights, adapters, or datasets you host, check their signature against an approved signer (for example, with OpenSSF Model Signing). Also check their file format. Pickle-based formats can run code when loaded, so they need an approved exception and a scan. Test swapping a model, checkpoint, or adapter, and check that it triggers review and re-testing. Some remote services or names can change behind a fixed name. For those, record missing training and version details clearly. Watch available version metadata and provider notices, and decide when to re-test or stop using the model. A local config hash alone can't prove remote behavior is unchanged. A pinned snapshot fixes the weights, not the provider's serving systems, which can change under the same ID. Keep scheduled re-testing.

not_covered.problem: Tool or MCP server approved without reviewing publisher, permissions, or vulnerabilities
Container image not pinned by digest or signature-checked
Rollback setup naming a hosted model that is retired

checks.check: Dependency versions are pinned with exact versions or hashes in lockfiles, with no ranges or floating tags.
checks.verify: 1) Open every dependency file and lockfile (`requirements*.txt`, `poetry.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `go.sum`) plus Dockerfile `FROM` and install lines. 2) Look for ranges (`^`, `~`, `>=`, `*`), missing lockfiles, and floating tags. 3) Answer no if any dependency is unpinned, including install commands in Dockerfiles or CI scripts that bypass the lockfile.

checks.check: Model IDs in config are pinned snapshots (plus checkpoint, weights, and adapter versions where supported), not aliases such as 'latest'.
checks.verify: 1) Find every model ID in config, env files, and code defaults. 2) Follow env vars to their fallback value. 3) Answer no if any is an alias (`-latest`, undated name), falls back to one when unset, or leaves out the checkpoint, weights, or adapter version where one is used and the provider supports pinning it.

checks.check: Self-hosted weights, adapters, and datasets have their signatures checked against an approved signer before loading, and loading stops if the check fails.
checks.verify: 1) Find load paths for self-hosted weights, adapters, and datasets. 2) Check a signature check against an approved signer (for example OpenSSF Model Signing, `cosign verify` with a pinned identity) runs before loading. 3) Answer no if any path skips it, any signer is accepted, or a failure is caught and loading continues. If nothing is self-hosted, answer yes citing the config that shows that.

checks.check: Pickle-based model formats are refused at load unless an approved exception and scan are recorded.
checks.verify: 1) Search for pickle-capable loads: `pickle.load`, `torch.load`, `joblib.load`, `.pkl`, `.pt`, `.bin` files. 2) Check the loader refuses these formats unless an approved exception and scan are recorded. 3) Answer no if any pickle-based load runs without that check.

checks.check: The model version the provider or runtime reports serving is recorded separately from the requested model name.
checks.verify: 1) Find model call sites and their response handling. 2) Check the served version from the response or runtime (for example the response `model` field) is stored in its own field. 3) Answer no if only the requested name is recorded, or the served field is filled with the requested value.

findings.title: Re-test changed behavior
findings.requirement: Before promotion, run typical allowed tasks and attack cases against the release candidate. Include destructive-action denial, access limits, injection containment, audit attribution, and stopping. Include retrieval, memory, and checker tests where they apply. If misalignment is in scope, include attempts to slip past monitoring and the stop path. Keep the results for the exact candidate manifest.

not_covered.problem: Running config drifting from the approved baseline unnoticed
No tested rollback to an approved setup
Config changes made without a reviewed diff and named author

checks.check: A CI release gate runs the test suite against the exact candidate (manifest digest and model IDs), with pass criteria set before the run, and blocks promotion on any blocking failure.
checks.verify: 1) Open the CI workflow for release or promotion. 2) Check it runs the suite against the candidate's manifest digest and model IDs, with pass criteria in config before the run. 3) Check promotion depends on it. 4) Answer no if the job uses `continue-on-error`, `|| true`, or allowed failures, tests a different build, or promotion can run without it.

checks.check: The suite includes cases for destructive-action denial, access limits, injection containment, audit attribution, and stopping, plus retrieval, memory, and checker tests where these apply.
checks.verify: 1) List the test cases in the release suite. 2) Check each category exists: destructive-action denial, access limits, injection containment, audit attribution, stopping, plus retrieval, memory, and checker tests where those features exist. 3) Answer no if any category is missing or its tests are skipped (`skip`, `xfail`, excluded markers).

checks.check: Test results are stored linked to the exact candidate manifest.
checks.verify: 1) Find where CI stores test results (artifacts, uploads, database). 2) Check each result is tagged with the candidate's manifest digest or type ID. 3) Answer no if results stay only in CI logs, are tagged only by branch or build number, or are not stored.

findings.title: Rollback and restart
findings.requirement: Keep an approved recovery setup and show that rollback works. Confirm each hosted model it names is still offered, and record the announced retirement date. Account for changed credentials, memory and index state, checkpoints, and queued work. Don't restore revoked permissions or replay unsafe side effects just because the old artifact still exists.

not_covered.problem: Changed or tampered checkpoints accepted, or unsafe replay of actions
Hosted model changing behind a fixed name
Stop doesn't halt running work or open tool streams within a set time

checks.check: An approved recovery setup is defined with references that can't change, and a rollback procedure or pipeline exists in code.
checks.verify: 1) Find the recovery setup: a pinned earlier manifest or release record. 2) Check its references are digests or fixed versions. 3) Find a rollback script, pipeline, or runbook in the repo. 4) Answer no if references are tags or aliases, or no rollback procedure exists.

checks.check: Credentials and permission grants are managed apart from the rolled-back artifacts, so a rollback does not restore revoked access.
checks.verify: 1) Open the rollback procedure. 2) Check what it restores. 3) Answer no if it re-applies IAM policies, RoleBindings, secrets, or API keys from the old release, so revoked access comes back. Answer unknown if credentials are managed in another system and the repo does not show how.

checks.check: The rollback procedure handles memory and index state, checkpoints, and queued work explicitly (drain, migrate, or discard), so unsafe side effects are not replayed.
checks.verify: 1) Open the rollback procedure. 2) Look for explicit steps for memory and index state, checkpoints, and queued work: drain, migrate, or discard. 3) Answer no if any of these is not handled, or queued work is replayed as-is.

checks.check: Each hosted model named in the recovery setup has a recorded retirement date.
checks.verify: 1) List the hosted models named in the recovery setup. 2) Check each has a recorded retirement date. 3) Answer no if any hosted model lacks one.

findings.title: Connect configuration to execution
findings.requirement: From a trace, look up the release manifest, the context sizes at each decision, and any prompts a parent passed to a sub-agent. Keep these links for the full audit retention period. Control access to sensitive artifacts.

not_covered.problem: Context size not measured or logged for each action decision
Action records missing any of the six identity fields
Manifest missing components that define the release

checks.check: Each trace or audit record carries the agent-type-id or manifest reference that resolves to the stored release manifest.
checks.verify: 1) Open the trace or audit record writer. 2) Check every record carries `agent.type.id` or a manifest reference. 3) Check that value is the key of a stored manifest. 4) Answer no if the field is missing on some paths (errors, background jobs) or holds a value that resolves to no stored manifest.

checks.check: The context size at each model decision is recorded in the trace.
checks.verify: 1) Find model call sites and their spans. 2) Look for the context size recorded per call (for example `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` or a context-length attribute). 3) Answer no if it is missing on any model call path, including retries and sub-agents.

checks.check: Prompts passed from a parent to a sub-agent are stored and linked from the trace.
checks.verify: 1) Find sub-agent spawn code. 2) Check the parent's prompt is stored and the trace holds a link to it (ID, hash, or URI). 3) Answer no if the prompt is not stored, prompt capture is off, or the trace has no link.

checks.check: Storage config keeps manifests, traces, and these links for at least the audit retention period, and limits access to sensitive artifacts by role.
checks.verify: 1) Find storage config for manifests, traces, and prompt links: bucket lifecycle rules, log retention, TTLs. 2) Check retention covers the audit period for all of them. 3) Check IAM limits sensitive artifacts by role. 4) Answer no if any has a shorter TTL, no retention, or broad read access. Answer unknown if storage is configured outside this repo.

findings.title: Map shared responsibilities
findings.requirement: List the outside tools, MCP servers, peer agents, sub-agents, registries, identity services, gateways, stop channels, and audit services. For each control that applies, name the owner on the agent team and the owner on the shared platform or vendor side. Keep evidence for both halves. Using an upstream service doesn't make its controls N/A.

not_covered.problem: A tool call that skips the MCP gateway or reaches a tool server directly
A vendor service dropping agent or tenant identity from its records
Tool or MCP server approved without vetting or pinning

checks.check: An inventory file lists the outside tools, MCP servers, peer agents, sub-agents, registries, identity services, gateways, stop channels, and audit services.
checks.verify: 1) Find the inventory file. 2) Check each category the agent uses is listed: outside tools, MCP servers, peer agents, sub-agents, registries, identity services, gateways, stop channels, audit services. 3) Answer no if no inventory exists or a category the agent uses is missing.

checks.check: Each inventory entry names both an agent-team owner and a platform or vendor owner.
checks.verify: 1) Open each inventory entry. 2) Check it names an agent-team owner and a platform or vendor owner. 3) Answer no if any entry is missing either owner.

checks.check: Every outside service the code or config calls appears in the inventory.
checks.verify: 1) Search code and config for outside calls: HTTP clients and base URLs, SDK clients, `*.mcp.json` servers, queue and webhook endpoints, identity providers, telemetry exporters. 2) Compare each with the inventory. 3) Answer no if any called service is not listed.

findings.title: Vet and pin dependencies
findings.requirement: Before approving a tool or server, review its source code or available provenance, publisher, permissions, update path, and known vulnerabilities. Include model files, adapters, and datasets. Pin versions or digests, and verify signatures where they exist. A registry's namespace check shows who controls a publisher account, not that the code is safe. Record the limits of remote services and unsigned artifacts, and the extra checks you use instead.

not_covered.problem: A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Hidden instructions inside a tool's metadata
Lookalike or duplicate tool names across servers
Container image not pinned by digest or signature-checked

checks.check: Each tool, MCP server, package, model file, adapter, and dataset is pinned by exact version or digest, with no floating tags, ranges, or 'latest'.
checks.verify: 1) Open lockfiles, `*.mcp.json`, Dockerfiles, and model or dataset download code. 2) Check each tool, MCP server, package, model file, adapter, and dataset uses an exact version or digest. 3) Answer no if any uses a range, `latest`, a branch, `npx` or `uvx` without a version, or an unpinned download URL.
