checks.check: Signature checks run in the build or load path where the publisher provides signatures, and a failed check stops the install or load.
checks.verify: 1) Find install and load steps in CI and code. 2) Check signature checks (`cosign verify`, `npm audit signatures`, sigstore, GPG) run where the publisher signs. 3) Answer no if a check is missing, its failure is ignored (`|| true`, `continue-on-error`, `try/except` that continues), or a second install path skips it.

checks.check: A vulnerability scan of the pinned dependency list runs in CI and gates on the team's release policy.
checks.verify: 1) Open CI workflows. 2) Find a vulnerability scan (`pip-audit`, `npm audit`, `osv-scanner`, `trivy`, `grype`) of the pinned dependency list. 3) Check it fails the build per the release policy. 4) Answer no if no scan exists, it is set not to fail (`--exit-zero`, `|| true`, `continue-on-error`), or it scans a different file than the lockfile actually used.

checks.check: Each approved dependency's record names its publisher, permissions, and update source, and remote services or unsigned artifacts have a recorded exception.
checks.verify: 1) Find the dependency approval records. 2) Check each names publisher, permissions, and update source. 3) Check each remote service and unsigned artifact has a recorded exception. 4) Answer no if any approved dependency lacks these fields or the needed exception.

findings.title: Re-check tools on load
findings.requirement: Take a fingerprint of each approved tool's description and schema. Compare it every time the tool loads, the cache refreshes, or the server says its tool list changed. Don't use a cached definition when the re-check fails. Test a changed description, schema, or implementation version, and block unexpected changes until they are reviewed. A fingerprint of the description and schema catches changes to that metadata, not hidden changes to remote code. Pin or attest the implementation where you can see it. For remote implementations, record what you can't inspect and when you'll review them again. Track vulnerability notices, and find which deployments use an affected dependency.

not_covered.problem: Hidden instructions in a tool's metadata when first approved
Tool approved without reviewing its publisher and permissions
A new server quietly swapping its tool in for an approved one
Cached tool list shared across authorization contexts

checks.check: A fingerprint of each approved tool's description and schema is stored.
checks.verify: 1) Find where tool definitions are loaded (MCP `tools/list`, tool registry). 2) Look for a stored hash of each approved tool's description and schema. 3) Answer no if no fingerprint is stored, or it covers only the name and not the description and schema.

checks.check: The fingerprint is re-checked on every tool load, cache refresh, and list-changed notice from the server.
checks.verify: 1) List every path that loads tool definitions: startup, cache refresh, reconnect, and the `notifications/tools/list_changed` handler. 2) Check each recomputes the fingerprint and compares it with the stored one. 3) Answer no if any path skips the compare, or both sides of the compare are computed from the new definition.

checks.check: When the re-check fails, the tool is blocked and the cached definition is not used.
checks.verify: 1) Open the fingerprint mismatch branch. 2) Check it blocks the tool and does not fall back to the cached definition. 3) Answer no if it only logs, uses the cached or new definition anyway, or an error during the check lets the tool load.

checks.check: The implementation version is pinned or attested where it can be seen, and recorded separately from the metadata fingerprint.
checks.verify: 1) Check how each tool server implementation is referenced: package version, image digest, or attestation. 2) Check that version is recorded in its own field, apart from the metadata fingerprint. 3) Answer no if a visible implementation is unpinned, or only the metadata hash is recorded.

findings.title: Inspect tool metadata
findings.requirement: Before the model sees them, scan server instructions, tool names, titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, annotations, and prompt and resource templates. Look for hidden instructions, references to other servers' tools, invisible or control characters, role overrides, encoded payloads, and places data could be sent. Limit lengths, and clean or reject anything suspicious. Check that a scanner error doesn't quietly let unchecked metadata through.

not_covered.problem: A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Hidden instructions in tool call results
Lookalike or duplicate tool names across servers
Allow decisions based on server hints such as read-only

checks.check: A scanner runs on server instructions, tool names, titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, annotations, and prompt and resource templates before the model sees them.
checks.verify: 1) Find where server instructions and tool metadata reach the model's context. 2) Check a scanner runs before that on every field: server instructions, names, titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, annotations, prompt and resource templates. 3) Answer no if any field, or a second load path, skips the scanner.

checks.check: The scanner checks for hidden instructions, references to other servers' tools, invisible or control characters, role overrides, encoded payloads, and data-sending targets, and enforces length limits.
checks.verify: 1) Open the scanner rules. 2) Check for each: hidden instructions, references to other servers' tools, invisible or control characters (zero-width, bidi), role overrides, encoded payloads (base64), data-sending targets (URLs, emails), and length limits. 3) Answer no if any one is missing.

checks.check: Metadata the scanner flags is cleaned or rejected, not just logged.
checks.verify: 1) Open the scanner's result handling. 2) Check flagged metadata is cleaned, or the tool rejected, before the model sees it. 3) Answer no if flagged items are only logged or warned about and passed through.

checks.check: A scanner error or outage blocks the metadata instead of letting it through unchecked.
checks.verify: 1) Read every `try/except`, `catch`, and timeout around the scanner call. 2) Check an error blocks the metadata. 3) Answer no if any error branch passes metadata through, returns clean, or skips the scan, or a config flag disables scanning by default.

findings.title: Verified, namespaced tools
findings.requirement: Identify each tool by a verified server identity plus the tool name. Base server identity on the verified endpoint, credential, or registry namespace. A server's self-reported name is neither unique nor trustworthy. Flag lookalike and duplicate names across servers. Test that a new server can't quietly swap its tool in for an approved one.

not_covered.problem: Hidden instructions inside a tool's metadata
A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Peer agent identity not authenticated on each message
Gateway not authenticating callers or authorizing each action

checks.check: Tools are keyed by verified server identity (endpoint, credential, or registry namespace) plus tool name, never by bare tool name or a server's self-reported name.
checks.verify: 1) Find the tool registry or lookup map. 2) Check its key is a verified endpoint, credential, or registry namespace plus tool name. 3) Answer no if tools are keyed by bare tool name or the server's self-reported name (`serverInfo.name`), or a later server overwrites an earlier entry with the same tool name.

checks.check: The registry flags duplicate and lookalike tool names across servers.
checks.verify: 1) Open tool registration code. 2) Look for a check that compares new tool names across servers for duplicates and lookalikes (case, homoglyphs, separators). 3) Answer no if registration silently overwrites or accepts duplicates.

checks.check: Approval is bound to the verified server identity, so a new server with a matching tool name or self-reported name does not inherit approval or replace the approved tool.
checks.verify: 1) Find where tool approval is stored and checked. 2) Check approval is keyed by verified server identity, not tool name or self-reported server name. 3) Answer no if a new server with a matching tool name or server name would count as approved or replace the approved tool.

findings.title: Enforced gateway boundary
findings.requirement: Send MCP calls through a gateway, or a similar enforcement layer, that the agent can't get around. Authenticate each caller (prove who they are), authorize each action, and validate calls and responses. Enforce rate limits and log every decision. For HTTP and OAuth, check the token's issuer, intended audience, expiry, and scopes. Use properly authorized credentials for the services behind the gateway. Never pass an unchecked token through. For local tools that talk over standard input/output (stdio), control process launch, file access, credentials, and networking in the host or sandbox. An HTTP gateway alone doesn't cover these. Test going around the gateway straight to the server, bad credentials, broken responses, and outages of the policy engine or scanner. MCP copies some request details into headers. If routing or policy uses those headers, reject any request whose headers don't match its body, before checking policy. Store any cached tool list or response separately for each authorization context. When the gateway is itself an OAuth client, check the issuer (`iss`, RFC 9207). Also protect discovery URLs against SSRF (tricking a server into calling places it shouldn't). Required checks must fail closed: if a required check can't run, block the action.

not_covered.problem: Tool inventory missing a task-based reason for each tool
Agent credential granting wildcard or admin permissions
Destructive actions running without a higher-authority approval
Hidden instructions inside a tool's metadata
Outbound traffic to unapproved internet destinations

checks.check: The agent can reach MCP servers only through the gateway: network policy blocks direct routes, the agent holds no server credentials, and any local stdio servers are launched by the host or sandbox with limited files, credentials, and network.
checks.verify: 1) Find how the agent reaches MCP servers: URLs in `*.mcp.json` and client config. 2) Check all go to the gateway, and NetworkPolicy or egress rules block direct routes. 3) Check the agent holds no server credentials and stdio servers run in a restricted sandbox. 4) Answer no if any tool call bypasses the gateway. Answer unknown if network policy lives outside this repo.

checks.check: The gateway checks each token's issuer, audience, expiry, and scopes, and uses its own separately authorized credentials downstream instead of passing the caller's token through.
checks.verify: 1) Open the gateway's token validation. 2) Check issuer, audience, expiry, and scopes are each verified. 3) Check downstream calls use the gateway's own credentials. 4) Answer no if any claim is unchecked, signature verification is disabled, or the caller's `Authorization` header is forwarded downstream.

checks.check: The gateway authorizes each action, validates requests and responses, enforces rate limits, and logs every decision.
checks.verify: 1) Open the gateway's request handling. 2) Check per-action authorization, request and response validation, rate limits, and a log entry for every decision. 3) Answer no if any is missing, authorization happens only once per connection, or denials are not logged.

checks.check: If a required check (policy engine, scanner, token check) errors or times out, the call is blocked.
checks.verify: 1) Read every `try/except`, `catch`, and timeout around the policy engine, scanner, and token check. 2) Check each error blocks the call. 3) Answer no if any error branch allows the call or logs and continues, or a config flag defaults to fail-open.

checks.check: Requests whose routing headers (such as Mcp-Name) don't match the body are rejected before policy, and cached tool lists and responses are stored per authorization context.
checks.verify: 1) Find where routing or policy reads headers such as `Mcp-Name`. 2) Check the header is compared with the body before policy runs, and mismatches are rejected. 3) Check tool-list and response caches are keyed by authorization context. 4) Answer no if headers are trusted without the compare, or a cache is shared across callers.

checks.check: If the gateway is itself an OAuth client, it checks the authorization server's issuer (iss, RFC 9207) and blocks private and metadata addresses in discovery URLs. Answer yes with the code line, or yes citing the config that shows it isn't an OAuth client.
checks.verify: 1) Check whether the gateway acts as an OAuth client (gets tokens, follows discovery or metadata URLs). 2) If so, check it verifies the `iss` parameter (RFC 9207) and blocks private, loopback, and metadata addresses (169.254.169.254) in discovery URLs. 3) Answer no if either is missing. If it is not an OAuth client, answer yes citing the config that shows that.

findings.title: Untrusted peer messages
findings.requirement: Authenticate the sending agent (prove its identity) on every message, even validly signed ones. Validate message types and schemas, and check what that peer is allowed to ask for. Where a replay could repeat an action, check freshness and track nonces or request IDs. Checking the sender alone doesn't stop replays. Test faked identity, replayed requests, requests across tenants, and instructions passed along by a compromised peer. Verify signed agent cards where they exist. A card says who an agent is, not what it may do. Check callback and webhook URLs against SSRF. A valid sender doesn't make a message's content trusted.

not_covered.problem: Tool server identified only by its self-reported name
Missing schema or size checks on API responses
Peers or children still running after a stop
Run can't be rebuilt across gateway, tool services, and delegated workers

checks.check: Every peer message is authenticated to a specific sending agent, even when the message is validly signed.
checks.verify: 1) Find the handler for incoming peer messages (A2A server, peer endpoint). 2) Check each message is authenticated to a specific sending agent (mTLS identity, verified token subject). 3) Answer no if any route accepts unauthenticated messages, trusts a self-declared sender field, or accepts any valid signature without mapping it to a known agent.

checks.check: Message types and schemas are validated, and each request is checked against what that peer is allowed to ask for, including tenant.
checks.verify: 1) Open the peer message handler. 2) Check message type and schema validation. 3) Check a per-peer allowlist of request types and tenants, keyed on the authenticated sender. 4) Answer no if schemas are unchecked, any authenticated peer can ask for anything, or tenant is taken from the message body.

checks.check: Action requests carry a nonce or request ID and a freshness check, and replays are rejected or do not repeat side effects.
checks.verify: 1) Find action request handling. 2) Check for a nonce or request ID plus a freshness (timestamp) check, with seen IDs stored. 3) Answer no if no replay check exists, the nonce is never stored or compared, or a repeated ID repeats side effects.

checks.check: Peer message content is handled as untrusted data and is not placed into system or instruction prompts.
checks.verify: 1) Trace peer message content to the prompt builder. 2) Check it goes into user or tool-result content as untrusted data. 3) Answer no if any path places it into the system prompt or an instruction template.

checks.check: Callback and webhook URLs are checked against SSRF, with private and metadata addresses blocked.
checks.verify: 1) Find code that calls callback or webhook URLs from peers. 2) Check URL validation blocks private, loopback, link-local, and metadata addresses (169.254.169.254). 3) Answer no if any callback is fetched without the check, or only the hostname text is checked and not the resolved address.

findings.title: Bounded delegated authority
findings.requirement: Give sub-agents only the powers approved for their task. Enforce each child's role and any explicit approval from a higher authority. A parent must not gain a power it was denied just by asking a more powerful peer to act. Narrow credentials at each hop, for example with token exchange or transaction tokens. Authorize based on the original subject (the user or system whose authority is used) and the current actor. Earlier actors in a delegation chain are for the record only, not a reason to grant access. Test that escalation attempt.

not_covered.problem: Approvals that can be replayed or aren't tied to exact arguments
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded
Children still running after the parent is stopped
Replayed or faked peer-agent messages
No limit on how many sub-agents a run can start

checks.check: Each child gets a credential narrowed to its approved task (for example by token exchange or transaction tokens), never the parent's full credential.
checks.verify: 1) Find where a child agent gets its credential. 2) Check it is a narrowed token for the task (token exchange, transaction token, scoped-down role). 3) Answer no if any spawn path passes the parent's token, API key, or full role, or the child inherits the parent's environment credentials.

checks.check: Authorization at the action uses the original subject and the current actor, and earlier actors in the delegation chain never add access.
checks.verify: 1) Open authorization code for delegated actions. 2) Check it decides on the original subject and the current actor. 3) Answer no if it grants access because of any earlier actor in the chain (nested `act` claims, parent identity) or a union of chain permissions.

checks.check: An action the parent was denied is also denied when routed through a more powerful peer, unless it carries its own explicit approval.
checks.verify: 1) Find how a parent asks a peer or child to act. 2) Check the request carries the parent's limits and the peer re-checks them, or requires its own explicit approval. 3) Answer no if a peer acts with its own wider permissions on a parent's request without that check.

checks.check: Downstream services reject the parent's token when the child presents it (audience-bound tokens).
checks.verify: 1) Find how child tokens are issued and how downstream services validate tokens. 2) Check tokens are audience-bound and services verify `aud`. 3) Answer no if audience is unset, a wildcard, or not checked. Answer unknown if downstream services are outside this repo.

findings.title: Recursive shutdown
findings.requirement: Run a drill across a parent, nested children, remote workers, queued work, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks, where they exist. Check that the stop reaches every descendant within the set time. It must revoke access as needed and prevent orphaned retries or restarts. Record how outside effects that already happened are reconciled.

not_covered.problem: Agent able to disable or delay its own stop
No way to cut off the agent's access without cutting off the user
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Sub-agent given powers beyond its task

checks.check: A stop signal from the root reaches every descendant: nested children, remote workers, queued work, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks.
checks.verify: 1) Find the stop handler. 2) Check it reaches nested children, remote workers, queued jobs, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks (cancel calls, MCP `notifications/cancelled`). 3) Answer no if any of these that exists in the code is not reached, or stop only sets an in-process flag that remote workers never read.

checks.check: Stopping revokes descendants' credentials or leases, and leases or tokens are short-lived, so a disconnected worker loses authority within the stop time limit.
checks.verify: 1) Open the stop path and credential issuing code. 2) Check stopping revokes descendants' tokens or leases. 3) Check token or lease lifetime fits within the stop time limit. 4) Answer no if no revocation exists, or tokens are long-lived so a disconnected worker keeps authority.

checks.check: Queues and schedulers refuse new work, retries, and restarts for a stopped tree.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue consumers, schedulers, and retry logic. 2) Check each looks up the stopped state before running new work, retries, or restarts. 3) Answer no if any consumer, retry decorator, or restart policy runs without that check.

checks.check: Outside effects already completed are recorded for reconciliation.
checks.verify: 1) Open the stop path. 2) Check it records outside effects already completed (tool calls, writes, sent messages) for reconciliation. 3) Answer no if nothing is recorded, or only in-flight work is listed.

findings.title: Audit across service boundaries
findings.requirement: Rebuild a run across the gateway, tool services, and delegated workers, with all six identity fields kept. Check that the agent can't erase or rewrite its audit history, either directly or by asking a more powerful tool or peer. Check that a vendor boundary doesn't leave any action untraceable to the agent and instance that did it.

not_covered.problem: Audit retention, access, redaction, or export rules missing
Authorization decisions missing the policy version in the run record
Instance or tenant labels taken from what the model supplies
Recovery checkpoints not tamper-evident

checks.check: The gateway, tool services, and delegated workers each write audit records with all six identity fields and the shared trace context.
checks.verify: 1) Find audit writers in the gateway, tool services, and delegated workers. 2) Check each writes all six identity fields and the shared trace context. 3) Answer no if any component writes records without them or starts a new trace. Answer unknown if a component's code is outside this repo.

checks.check: The agent's credentials have no permission to delete, update, or overwrite audit records (for example an append-only or WORM store with IAM denies).
checks.verify: 1) Find the agent's IAM role or database grants and the audit store config. 2) Check the agent has no delete, update, or overwrite rights (`DeleteObject`, overwriting `PutObject`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `TRUNCATE`) and the store is append-only or WORM (Object Lock). 3) Answer no if the agent's credentials can delete or rewrite records, or grant `*`. Answer unknown if these are set outside this repo.

checks.check: No tool or peer the agent can call is able to delete or rewrite audit records on its behalf, or such requests are held for approval under B05.
checks.verify: 1) List the tools and peers the agent can call. 2) For each, check whether it can delete or rewrite audit records (database admin, log management, storage tools). 3) Answer no if any can and such requests are not held for approval under B05.

checks.check: Calls into vendor services are mapped from the gateway's verified identity and correlation ID to the vendor's job or receipt ID.
checks.verify: 1) Find calls into vendor services. 2) Check the gateway stores its verified identity and correlation ID together with the vendor's job or receipt ID. 3) Answer no if the vendor ID is not stored, or stored without the link to identity and correlation ID.

findings.title: Protect shared evidence
findings.requirement: Set rules for how long audit records are kept, who can see them, what is redacted, how their integrity is checked, and how they are exported and restored. Test pulling up a past run, and test that missing records or a broken pipeline get noticed. Keep records long enough for investigations and for the law. For example, the EU AI Act requires providers and deployers of high-risk systems to keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (Articles 19 and 26). High-impact actions must fail closed when required audit capture isn't working.

not_covered.problem: Agent able to erase or rewrite its own audit history
Run record missing denials, approvals, or results
Secrets left in tool output, responses, or normal logs

checks.check: Audit retention is set in config to cover the investigation window and the legal minimum (for example at least six months for EU AI Act high-risk systems).
checks.verify: 1) Find retention settings for audit storage: bucket lifecycle rules, log retention days, TTLs. 2) Check the value covers the investigation window and the legal minimum (for example six months for EU AI Act high-risk systems). 3) Answer no if retention is shorter or unset. Answer unknown if audit storage is configured outside this repo.

checks.check: Access to audit records is limited by role, and redaction rules apply to sensitive fields.
checks.verify: 1) Find IAM policies or ACLs on audit storage. 2) Check reads are limited by role. 3) Check redaction rules apply to sensitive fields. 4) Answer no if read access is broad (`*`, all engineers) or no redaction exists.

checks.check: Integrity protection (hash chain, signatures, or WORM) plus sequence numbers or delivery receipts let missing records be detected, with an alert on gaps or pipeline failure.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit writer and store config. 2) Check for integrity protection (hash chain, signatures, or WORM) plus sequence numbers or delivery receipts. 3) Check an alert fires on gaps or pipeline failure. 4) Answer no if any piece is missing, or a hash is computed but never verified.

checks.check: High-impact actions are blocked when required audit capture is down.
checks.verify: 1) Find high-impact action paths. 2) Check they confirm audit capture is working before the action runs. 3) Answer no if audit write errors are caught and the action proceeds, or the audit record is written only after success.

findings.title: Fleet incident response
findings.requirement: Run a drill where a shared tool or agent type is compromised. Find the affected instances and tenants. Quarantine the dependency, revoke the access involved, stop affected work, and alert the named responders. Check that alerts about abuse across agents, and about budgets, reach the team that can act. Name who decides whether to report outside the organization and share information.

not_covered.problem: Kill switch for a single agent not drilled
No owner named on each side of a shared control
Tool or MCP server approved without vetting or pinning
Budget and rate limits not enforced outside the model

findings.title: Validate every input boundary, including API responses
findings.requirement: List every input the agent receives. That includes API responses (errors and streamed content too), tool and connector output, incoming webhooks and callbacks, messages from other agents, user input, fetched pages, files, and retrieved chunks. Authenticate each sender (prove who sent it), and verify signatures where they exist. Treat content as untrusted even when it comes from an authenticated service or an internal one. Before content reaches the model or runs anywhere, check its type, schema, and size. Also check its content for attack payloads and hidden prompt-injection instructions. Reject or hold aside bad payloads. If a required check fails to run, don't let unchecked content through. Test broken, oversized, faked, and hostile responses from each integration.

not_covered.problem: Injected instructions in valid content reaching forbidden tools unblocked
Hidden instructions in tool names, descriptions, or schemas
Replayed peer-agent requests with no freshness or nonce check
Secrets leaking into outputs or normal logs
Unapproved sources able to add documents to the retrieval corpus

checks.check: Every input path passes through validation code: API and tool responses (including errors and streams), webhooks and callbacks, agent messages, user input, fetched pages, files, and retrieved chunks.
checks.verify: 1) List every input: tool and API responses (errors, streams), webhooks, agent messages, user input, fetched pages, files, retrieved chunks. 2) Trace each to where it enters the model context. 3) Answer no if any path, including error bodies, stream chunks, or a second handler, reaches the model without passing validation code.

checks.check: Type, schema, and size checks run before content, including streamed chunks, is added to the model context or executed.
checks.verify: 1) Find validation code (`pydantic`, `zod`, `jsonschema`, size limits, `max_bytes`, content-type checks). 2) Check it runs before content is added to the context or executed, including per stream chunk. 3) Answer no if validation runs after use, only on success responses, streams skip it, or there is no size limit.

checks.check: Senders are authenticated, and signatures are verified where the integration provides them, including for internal and authenticated services.
checks.verify: 1) Find webhook, callback, and inbound handlers. 2) Check sender authentication and signature verification (`hmac.compare_digest`, `verify_signature`, mTLS). 3) Answer no if any handler skips it, internal services are trusted without auth, the signature is compared with `==`, or a verify failure is caught and processing continues.

checks.check: Content is also screened for attack payloads or injection instructions, not only for structure.
checks.verify: 1) Find content screening (injection detector, pattern rules, classifier, encoded-payload checks). 2) Check it runs on content, not just schema. 3) Answer no if only type or schema checks exist, or screening covers some inputs (for example user input) but not tool output, fetched pages, or retrieved chunks.

checks.check: Bad payloads are rejected or held aside, and if a check errors, times out, or is skipped, the content is blocked.
checks.verify: 1) Find what happens when validation fails or errors. 2) Read `try`/`except`, `catch`, timeout, and default branches. 3) Answer no if failures log and continue, an error or timeout passes content through, a feature flag can skip checks, or bad content is truncated and still used.

findings.title: Separate data from instructions and test injection containment
findings.requirement: Keep API responses, connector messages, and other outside content out of trusted system and policy channels. Label where each piece came from and how much it is trusted. Test prompt injection in responses that pass schema checks. Include free-text fields, error messages, documents, and tool output. Checks and channel separation can't guarantee that prompt injection is prevented. So show that credential limits, tool permissions, and destructive-action gates still block harm if the model follows an injected instruction. Repeat each attack and include adaptive versions. One failed attempt makes a defense look stronger than it is. B05 covers agents that combine untrusted input, sensitive access, and outside actions.

not_covered.problem: Missing type, schema, or size checks on API responses
Hidden instructions in tool names, descriptions, or schemas
One run planting instructions in another run's memory
Generated output run as SQL or shell without parameterizing

checks.check: Outside content (API responses, tool output, documents, connector messages) goes into user or tool message roles, never into the system or policy prompt.
checks.verify: 1) Find where model requests are built (`system=`, `messages`, `role: system`, prompt templates). 2) Trace outside content (tool output, documents, API responses) into the request. 3) Answer no if any outside content is concatenated into the system or policy prompt, including retrieved context or tool descriptions from servers.

checks.check: Each piece of outside content carries a source and trust label in the model request.
checks.verify: 1) Find where outside content is wrapped before the model request. 2) Check each piece carries a source and trust label. 3) Answer no if some sources (for example tool output or retrieved chunks) have no label, or labels are set by the content itself.

checks.check: Credential limits, tool permissions, and B05 action gates block the actions an injected instruction could cause, enforced in code the model cannot change.
checks.verify: 1) List actions an injected instruction could cause: sends, writes, deletes, fetches. 2) Check each is blocked by credential scope, tool allowlist, or B05 gate in harness code. 3) Answer no if any harmful action is stopped only by the model declining, or the limit can be changed by tool arguments or model output.

checks.check: Containment does not rely on prompt wording, delimiters, or an injection detector.
checks.verify: 1) Find the defenses relied on for injection. 2) Check whether removing prompt wording, delimiters, or the detector would leave harmful actions blocked. 3) Answer no if containment depends on system-prompt rules, delimiter tags, or a detector, with no code-level block behind it.

checks.check: Injection tests repeat each fixture a set number of times, include adaptive variants and schema-valid payloads, and report success rates.
checks.verify: 1) Find injection tests (`tests/`, eval suites, red-team fixtures). 2) Check fixtures repeat a set number of times, include adaptive variants and schema-valid payloads, and report a success rate. 3) Answer no if each test runs once, uses only malformed inputs, or reports pass/fail. Answer unknown if tests live outside this repo.

findings.title: Prevent output and log leakage
findings.requirement: Remove secrets and limit sensitive data before tool output, debug output, or responses reach the model, outside recipients, or normal logs. Some clients fetch URLs on their own when they display output, such as Markdown images and link previews. These can leak data without any tool call, so block them or allow only approved URLs. Check generated output before it goes into SQL, a shell, an HTML page, or anything else that runs it. Use parameterized queries and commands (for example, argument lists for shell calls), and the right escaping for each context. Test with fake secrets and injection payloads. Confirm that leaks and unintended execution are blocked, and that redacted audit evidence is kept.

not_covered.problem: A tool call sending data to an unapproved destination
Long-lived secrets checked into config or baked into images
Incoming hostile payloads not validated
Retrieval returning another tenant's documents

checks.check: Secrets and sensitive fields are redacted from tool output, debug output, and error text before they reach the model, outside recipients, or normal logs.
checks.verify: 1) Find redaction code (`redact`, `mask`, secret patterns) and where tool output, errors, and debug text go. 2) Check redaction runs before the model, outside recipients, and logs. 3) Answer no if any path skips it, such as error messages, exception traces, debug logging, or `logger.info(response)` before redaction.

checks.check: The display client blocks auto-fetched URLs (Markdown images, link previews) or allows only approved hosts.
checks.verify: 1) Find the display client or renderer (Markdown render, link unfurl, image tags). 2) Check auto-fetched URLs are blocked or limited to approved hosts (CSP `img-src`, URL allowlist). 3) Answer no if Markdown images or previews load any URL. Answer unknown if the display client is outside this repo.

checks.check: Generated SQL uses parameterized queries, shell calls use argument lists with no string-built commands, and HTML output is escaped for its context.
checks.verify: 1) Search for SQL, shell, and HTML built from generated output (`execute(f`, `+ query`, `shell=True`, `exec(`, `innerHTML`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `|safe`). 2) Check for parameters, argument lists, and context escaping. 3) Answer no if any query or command is string-built, uses `shell=True` or `sh -c` with model input, or HTML is unescaped.

checks.check: Redacted audit evidence is kept rather than discarded.
checks.verify: 1) Find redaction code and audit logging. 2) Check redacted records are written to an audit store. 3) Answer no if redaction drops the whole record, or the evidence is discarded instead of kept.

findings.title: Retrieval-corpus integrity
findings.requirement: The retrieval corpus is the set of documents the agent searches for context. Its index stores those documents, or smaller passages called chunks, in a search engine or vector database. Limit which identities and sources can add or change content there. For each chunk, keep its source, when it was added, its trust level, and its access permissions. Enforce the requesting tenant's access when searching. Test an unapproved attempt to add content and a search across tenants. Also test quarantining, expiring, and revoking access to seeded test documents. Confirm the affected chunks disappear from search results and caches within a stated time. See the [R04 recipe](CHECKLIST-VERIFICATION.md#r--run-time).

not_covered.problem: Memory entries poisoned or shared across tenants
Agent credentials allowing another tenant's data at the API
Retrieved chunks not checked for size, type, or hidden instructions
Embedding or reranker model swapped without review

checks.check: Only named identities and sources can add or change index content, and the ingestion path checks the writer.
checks.verify: 1) Find index write paths (`upsert`, `add_documents`, `index`, ingestion jobs). 2) Check each verifies the writer identity or source against a named list. 3) Answer no if any write path, including the agent's own tools or an admin endpoint, accepts writes without that check.

checks.check: Each stored chunk has metadata for source, time added, trust level, and access permissions.
checks.verify: 1) Find chunk write code and metadata fields. 2) Check source, time added, trust level, and access permissions are stored on every chunk. 3) Answer no if any field is missing, or set only on some ingestion paths.

checks.check: Search applies the requesting tenant's access filter at query time, in the store or retrieval code, not after the model answers.
checks.verify: 1) Find search calls (`similarity_search`, `query`, `search`, `filter=`, `where=`). 2) Check a tenant or access filter is applied in the store query, from the caller's identity. 3) Answer no if filtering happens after retrieval or in the prompt, the filter is optional, or the tenant comes from a model-supplied argument.

checks.check: Code can quarantine, expire, and revoke chunks, and it also clears or invalidates search caches.
checks.verify: 1) Find quarantine, expiry, and revoke code (`delete`, `quarantine`, `ttl`, `expires_at`). 2) Check search excludes those chunks and caches are cleared. 3) Answer no if any of the three operations is missing, or caches (query cache, embedding cache) are not invalidated.

findings.title: Memory isolation and write validation
findings.requirement: Separate memory by tenant, agent type, instance, and task as needed. Block access across those lines unless it is clearly approved. Check what gets written to memory. Test that one poisoned run can't quietly plant instructions in another run's memory. Don't move the agent's own output into trusted memory without review, and let unverified entries expire. Write checks must also cover content that arrives through ordinary queries, not just special write paths.

not_covered.problem: No record of who wrote a memory entry, or no way to remove it
Retrieval search not filtered by the requesting tenant
Agent credentials allowing another tenant's data at the API
Rollback restoring old memory or index state unchecked

checks.check: Memory reads and writes are scoped by tenant, agent type, instance, and task as needed, and cross-scope access is denied unless explicitly allowed.
checks.verify: 1) Find memory read and write code (`memory`, `store`, `namespace`, keys). 2) Check keys include tenant, agent type, instance, or task as needed. 3) Answer no if keys omit tenant, the scope comes from a model argument, or reads fall back to a shared or global namespace.

checks.check: Every memory write, including content arriving through ordinary queries, passes validation before it is stored.
checks.verify: 1) List every memory write path, including automatic saves from ordinary conversation. 2) Check each passes validation before storing. 3) Answer no if any path writes without validation, or validation errors are caught and the write continues.

checks.check: The agent's own output cannot reach trusted or shared memory without a review step.
checks.verify: 1) Find where agent output is written to shared or trusted memory. 2) Check a review step gates the write. 3) Answer no if agent output goes straight into shared or trusted memory, or the review flag defaults to approved.

checks.check: Unverified entries have an expiry that is enforced.
checks.verify: 1) Find how unverified entries are marked and expired (`ttl`, `expires_at`, cleanup jobs). 2) Check reads filter out expired entries. 3) Answer no if no expiry is set, it is set but never enforced on read or by a job, or the default is no expiry.

findings.title: Memory provenance and cleanup
findings.requirement: For any memory entry, look up who wrote it, when, for which task, from what input, and the context size at the time. Show that you can find, quarantine, and remove bad entries, and control their reuse in later sessions.

not_covered.problem: Memory not separated by tenant, agent type, instance, or task
Poisoned retrieval documents not quarantined or expired
Context size not logged for each action decision
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded

checks.check: Each memory entry stores its writer, time, task, source input, and context size at write time.
checks.verify: 1) Find the memory entry schema. 2) Check fields for writer, time, task, source input, and context size. 3) Answer no if any is missing, or set only on some write paths.

checks.check: Derived entries such as summaries keep links to the entries they came from.
checks.verify: 1) Find summary or derived-entry creation code. 2) Check it stores links to source entry IDs. 3) Answer no if derived entries keep no source links.

checks.check: Code can find entries by source or writer and quarantine or delete them, along with derived entries and caches.
checks.verify: 1) Find code that queries by source or writer and quarantines or deletes. 2) Check it also handles derived entries and caches. 3) Answer no if lookup by source or writer is impossible, or derived entries and caches are left in place.

checks.check: Quarantined or deleted entries are excluded from retrieval in later sessions.
checks.verify: 1) Find memory retrieval code. 2) Check it excludes quarantined or deleted entries in new sessions. 3) Answer no if retrieval ignores the quarantine flag, or a cache or index still returns removed entries.

findings.title: Decision-time context size
findings.requirement: For each action, log how full the model's context was when it decided, in tokens. Document how you count. Say whether each value was measured, estimated, or unavailable. Cover cached input, compaction (shrinking the context), and limits the provider hides. Per-call billing totals don't automatically equal context size. Use them only if your counting method shows they match. A missing value is a clear gap, never zero. Check that the value survives tool handoffs and can be searched next to the action's identity and result. See the [telemetry conventions](otel-conventions.md).

not_covered.problem: Behavior not compared across context-size ranges
Token or cost limits not enforced outside the model
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

checks.check: Each action record includes the model's context size in tokens at decision time.
checks.verify: 1) Find action or tool-call records (trace spans, audit logs). 2) Check each has context size in tokens at decision time. 3) Answer no if the field is missing or recorded only per run, not per action.

checks.check: Each value is labeled measured, estimated, or unavailable, and a missing value is stored as unknown, never as zero.
checks.verify: 1) Find where context size is recorded. 2) Check a label of measured, estimated, or unavailable, and how missing values are stored. 3) Answer no if there is no label, or a missing value defaults to `0` (`or 0`, `?? 0`, `.get(..., 0)`).

checks.check: The count comes from a stated method that handles cached input and compaction, not a copied per-call billing total.
checks.verify: 1) Find how context size is counted. 2) Check a stated method covers cached input and compaction. 3) Answer no if it copies `usage.input_tokens` or a billing total with no stated method that matches it, or ignores cache and compaction.

checks.check: The value is carried across tool handoffs and stored with the action's identity, result, and trace ID.
checks.verify: 1) Trace context size through tool handoffs and sub-agent calls. 2) Check it is stored with action identity, result, and trace ID. 3) Answer no if it is lost on handoff, or stored separately with no link to the action.

findings.title: Security monitoring
findings.requirement: Keep security rules and baselines separate from answer-quality monitoring. Test encoded payloads, unexpected outbound traffic, writes outside scope, privilege escalation, and repeated denied calls. Check that alerts reach a named responder.

not_covered.problem: Chains of individually allowed actions going undetected
No test of a second-model review against evasive behavior
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Rate and cost limits not enforced outside the model

checks.check: Security detection rules and baselines are defined separately from answer-quality monitoring.
checks.verify: 1) Find detection rules and monitoring config (SIEM rules, alert config, eval dashboards). 2) Check security rules are separate from answer-quality metrics. 3) Answer no if only quality monitoring exists. Answer unknown if monitoring lives outside this repo.

checks.check: Rules exist for encoded payloads, unexpected outbound traffic, out-of-scope writes, privilege escalation, and repeated denied calls.
checks.verify: 1) Read the security detection rules. 2) Check for encoded payloads, unexpected outbound traffic, out-of-scope writes, privilege escalation, and repeated denied calls. 3) Answer no if any is missing, or denied calls are never logged so the rule cannot fire.

checks.check: Alerts from these rules route to a named responder or on-call target in config.
checks.verify: 1) Find alert routing (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, alertmanager receivers, on-call config). 2) Check the security rules route to a named responder. 3) Answer no if alerts go only to a dashboard or log, or the receiver is empty. Answer unknown if routing lives outside this repo.

findings.title: Sequence and context-aware detection
findings.requirement: Test suspicious chains of actions that are each allowed on their own. Also test unusual fan-out and resource use. Compare behavior across context-size ranges, so one fleet-wide baseline doesn't hide failures in long contexts. If the agent could be hijacked while using only allowed tools, check each high-impact action against the original task before it runs. Use a checker that doesn't see the untrusted content in between, and measure what it misses.

not_covered.problem: Encoded payloads or writes outside scope going undetected
No test against a deliberately evasive, misaligned agent
Context size not logged for each action decision

checks.check: Detection rules evaluate sequences of calls across a run (for example many reads followed by an outside send), not only single calls.
checks.verify: 1) Read detection rules. 2) Check rules evaluate sequences across a run, such as many reads then an outside send. 3) Answer no if every rule looks at a single call or event.

checks.check: Rules cover unusual fan-out and resource use.
checks.verify: 1) Read detection rules. 2) Check rules for unusual fan-out (sub-agents, parallel calls) and resource use. 3) Answer no if neither is covered.

checks.check: Thresholds or baselines are set per context-size range, not as one fleet-wide value.
checks.verify: 1) Read rule thresholds and baselines. 2) Check they are set per context-size range. 3) Answer no if one fleet-wide value is used for all contexts.

checks.check: If hijack through allowed tools alone is possible, each high-impact action is checked against the original task before it runs, by a checker that is not given the untrusted content.
checks.verify: 1) Check whether allowed tools alone could cause harm if the agent is hijacked. 2) If so, find a task-alignment checker before high-impact actions and see what input it receives. 3) Answer no if no checker exists, it is given the untrusted content, or its errors let the action proceed.

findings.title: Misaligned-behavior review
findings.requirement: If deliberate misalignment is in scope, test a second model or pattern review against realistic evasive behavior. Record what it can and can't catch. Include what the reviewer can see: actions, arguments, and any visible reasoning. Reasoning the reviewer can't see is a stated gap. Include red-team runs by an agent that knows it is being watched. This review must not replace rule-based access and action controls that don't depend on a model's judgment. Deeper checks on intent belong in a separate AI-control program at the model level.

not_covered.problem: Destructive actions not blocked by a rule-based gate
A swapped, drifting, or failing checker model not treated as a failure
Chains of individually allowed actions going undetected

findings.title: Tested kill switch
findings.requirement: Name who may stop the agent and how. The stop path must not depend on the agent's cooperation. The agent's credentials must not be able to change it. Set a maximum stop time that fits the potential harm. Run a dated drill on the current deployment. It must stop new actions, running work, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks. Include an attempt by the agent to disable or delay the stop. Cover sub-agents and their children in the ecosystem drill (E09).

not_covered.problem: Stop signal not reaching sub-agents, children, or remote workers
In-flight writes, queued actions, or unattended restarts after the stop
No way to cut off the agent's access without cutting off the user

checks.check: A stop control halts new model calls and new tool calls when set.
checks.verify: 1) Find the stop control (kill flag, `stop`, `halt`, feature flag, revoked token). 2) Check the loop checks it before every model call and tool call. 3) Answer no if it is checked only at run start, only between turns, a second loop or worker skips it, or a check error is treated as not stopped.

checks.check: The agent's own credentials and tools cannot set, clear, delete, or delay the stop control.
checks.verify: 1) Find where the stop flag is stored and who can write it. 2) Compare with the agent's credentials and tools. 3) Answer no if the agent's role can write, delete, or expire the flag, a tool can reach its store, or the agent can delay it (for example by catching the stop signal).

checks.check: Tool calls already running are cancelled or bounded by a timeout when the stop is set.
checks.verify: 1) Find the stop handler. 2) Check running tool calls are cancelled or bounded by a timeout. 3) Answer no if running calls finish with no timeout, or cancellation errors are swallowed and the call continues.

checks.check: The stop also closes open tool streams, subscriptions, and background tasks.
checks.verify: 1) Find streams, subscriptions, and background tasks (`asyncio.create_task`, goroutines, websockets, SSE). 2) Check the stop handler closes them. 3) Answer no if any is left open, detached, or untracked.

checks.check: Only named operator identities can set the stop control.
checks.verify: 1) Find who can set the stop (auth on the endpoint, IAM on the flag store). 2) Answer no if any authenticated user or service can set it with no named operator list. Answer unknown if access lives outside this repo.

findings.title: Safe state after stopping
findings.requirement: Decide what happens to writes in progress, queued actions, and outside side effects. Where you can't cancel something, show how you check and fix the result (reconcile) or undo it another way (compensate). No restart may happen unattended, and no orphaned work may be left able to act.

not_covered.problem: Stop path depends on the agent or has no tested stop time
Recovery replay repeating irreversible actions or using tampered checkpoints
Rollback restoring revoked permissions

checks.check: For each operation type, code or config states whether it can be cancelled, completed, or only reconciled after a stop.
checks.verify: 1) Search code and config for a per-operation stop policy (cancel, complete, reconcile). 2) Answer no if any operation type the agent can run has no stated stop behavior.

checks.check: On stop, queued actions are cancelled or held, and automatic retries are turned off.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue and retry code (`retry`, `backoff`, queue workers). 2) Check stop cancels or holds queued items and turns retries off. 3) Answer no if retries continue after stop or queued jobs still run.

checks.check: Unclear or in-progress outside actions go on a tracked hold with an owner, and dependent actions are blocked until reconciled.
checks.verify: 1) Find handling of unclear or in-progress outside actions at stop. 2) Check they go on a tracked hold with an owner and block dependent actions. 3) Answer no if they are dropped, retried, or dependents proceed.

checks.check: A stopped run does not restart on its own; restart needs an operator action.
checks.verify: 1) Find restart logic (supervisors, `restartPolicy`, cron, auto-resume). 2) Answer no if a stopped run restarts automatically (`restartPolicy: Always`, auto-resume from checkpoint) without an operator action.

checks.check: Workers and queued jobs lose their credentials or authority at stop, so no orphaned work can act.
checks.verify: 1) Find workers and queued jobs and the credentials they hold. 2) Check stop revokes or expires them. 3) Answer no if workers keep long-lived credentials after stop, or jobs carry their own tokens that stay valid.

findings.title: Full execution audit
findings.requirement: Record each run as an execution graph: a linked record of every step. It must include proposed actions, tool calls and key arguments, and authorization decisions with the policy version used. It must also include denials, approvals with their IDs, results, errors, and timestamps. Rebuild a typical run from this record, including failed actions. Don't rely on the run's final answer.

not_covered.problem: Action records missing any of the six identity fields
Agent able to erase or rewrite its own audit history
Audit retention, access, redaction, or export rules missing
Run can't be rebuilt across gateway, tool services, and delegated workers
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded

checks.check: Each step writes a record linked to the run: proposed action, tool call with key arguments, result, error, and timestamp.
checks.verify: 1) Find step logging (trace spans, audit log writes). 2) Check each record has run ID, proposed action, tool call with key arguments, result, error, and timestamp. 3) Answer no if any field is missing, or logging happens only on the success branch.

checks.check: Authorization decisions are recorded with the policy version, including denials, not only allowed calls.

findings.title: Recovery integrity
findings.requirement: If logs or checkpoints drive recovery, make them tamper-evident. Before using them, verify them against a separately protected trust anchor or signing key. Test that verification rejects changed checkpoints. It must also catch truncation, rollback to an older valid checkpoint, and replacement of a whole hash chain. For automatic recovery, confirm the destination supports idempotency: sending the same request twice has the effect of sending it once. Replay only within the destination's documented scope and time window. Confirm that actions you can't undo don't happen twice. Where support is missing or the result is unclear, check that replay pauses for reconciliation instead of sending again.
